lines: Skills Acrobatics +5, Perception +3, Stealth +5 Senses Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 13 Languages None

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Skills Perception +3, Stealth +4 Senses passive Perception 13 Languages —

gm.title: Traits
lines: Keen Hearing and Smell. The wolf has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell. Pack Tactics. The wolf has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the wolf’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 11 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Skills Perception +5, Stealth +4 Senses Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 15 Languages None

gm.title: Traits
lines: Pack Tactics. The wolf has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the wolf’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn’t have the Incapacitated condition.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

name: A bag with a forwarding address

gm.title: At the table
lines: Objects put in a bag appear in a former owner's washbasin. The washbasin keeper has begun labeling and selling the arrivals.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Grain runs short before winter. A retired ovensweeper who buys kiln ash to repair old mortar remembers bricking up the municipal grain store behind a bake oven. They will show the party where if the city promises to pay for the repairs.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An honest ally switches sides when an enemy buys their debt. Make their change of allegiance negotiable and let the party learn the terms.

name: A bargain with nobody left to collect

gm.title: At the table
lines: A villain keeps a borrowed talent until the other party receives the agreed payment. Find the lawful successor and ask whether they want the bargain fulfilled or renegotiated.

name: A basket full of unripe berries

gm.title: At the table
lines: Foragers are stripping a patch before its fruit is ready. Their village expects a hard frost and needs news from the weather tower.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The same light is an invitation on the way out and a distress call on the way back. A lighthouse keeper will share the signal book if the party helps repair the boat that takes them off shift.

name: A bell auction chooses who rings the thaw

gm.title: At the table
lines: The winning bidder rings in spring. Any fishing boat within earshot can launch that day without paying. The old bell has cracked and the new one can be heard from the disputed island, where the regular fee is still contested. Players can help decide whether to move it, repair the old bell, or require two signals.

name: A bellows draws in the marsh

gm.title: At the table
lines: One room smells of peat when a forge operates even though every chimney exits uphill. Pull the bellows when the forge is cold. Wet reeds catch on its intake grate. Behind the grate a broad duct descends to a flooded passage.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wild boar uproots a strip of plants while ignoring all the others. A forager demonstrates how it is following a buried edible root.

name: A bone key leaves a debt

gm.title: At the table
lines: A key opens a single lock and breaks in it. Owners of locks opened this way can use the fragment to ask who turned it, which makes the key useful evidence as well as a shortcut.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Names disappear from a log while titles and salaries remain. A set of signed expense sheets can reconstruct who held each job.

name: A book moth connects two borrowers’ copies

gm.title: At the table
lines: Overnight the moth stitches together the first sheets of two books once owned by the same reader. A missing leaf was torn out of one of them. Follow the twitching thread before dawn to find where the moth tucked it.

name: A borrowed sled makes you responsible for its next passenger

gm.title: At the table
lines: The sled carries a visible customs token. Anyone traveling on it inherits responsibility for taking the next registered traveler through a checkpoint. Check who put a particular passenger on the list before getting underway.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bad smell rises only while the waterwheel turns. The miller will stop it if the party handles today's line of impatient customers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A proud brewer lets rivals name one missing ingredient before serving. One rival names a crop the council forbade planting last season.

name: A bulette waits for the loaded sledge

gm.title: At the table
lines: Fresh upheavals follow the tandem ruts, ending where a sledge was unloaded. The creature surfaces before the next loaded crossing. Move the supplies in smaller loads, use the bedrock shoulder, or send an empty sledge while someone watches where the ground moves.

name: A burning beard marks last call

gm.title: At the table
lines: A landlord sets a magical flame alight for the final round. Tonight it burns low and blue after the firewood merchant arrives.

name: A buyer wants the old dents left in

gm.title: At the table
lines: A collector seeks family ornaments pawned during a bad winter and pays extra to keep two characteristic dents visible. A stoneworker can match the marks to a setting tool still used in one atelier. The repair book can lead to the buyers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Local travelers leave carved signs to say whether the camp is safe. Someone added a fresh sign upside down.

name: A canceled debt still guarantees someone else’s loan

gm.title: At the table
lines: The party can erase a local worker’s debt by tearing up its contract. A note in the margin shows that the debt also backs a ferry repair loan. Bring both parties to the lender to substitute a different guarantee, or let the cancellation stand and help the ferry find another source of credit.

name: A cart with one coffin too many

gm.title: At the table
lines: The burial clerk counts fewer names than crates. The driver wants someone's help tracing the delivery while keeping the horses moving.

name: A cat inhabits the fish scale

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cat ghost inhabits the counter scale at a fishmonger's stall. Let the party decide whether to spend a morning giving it the ordinary care nobody gave it in life.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A temporary illusion puts a mask on the drinker. It silently takes on the expression of whoever last handled the vial. The wearer can use a mirror to see what that person felt.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hungry child offers buttons to be escorted to a cookshop after dusk. The shopkeeper recognizes the buttons as tokens for staff meals.

name: A cistern frog keeps its understudy

gm.title: At the table
lines: One frog dives when the kitchen bell rings, and another calls while the first is underwater. The kitchen crew can tell which is calling. A stranger who tries to slip across the yard between calls hears a third frog answering under the floor.

name: A city's night shift mislays its sunrise

gm.title: At the table
lines: Lamplighters argue over who should extinguish their last street when an artificial dawn starts halfway through the shift. Ask where it ends and follow the contiguous lit street to the device being tested, or help the workers make a temporary handover.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The elders can sweep an old influence past a ring of doors. Draw where the boundary will land and ask what it leaves outside.

name: A cold hand on warm wax

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hand feels cold enough to firm warm wax on contact. The cooling ends after it has set one small seal.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A garrison's oath has lost its divine witness. Officers claim it still holds, while rank-and-file soldiers want a new agreement they can read before signing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An argument spills from a table to a packed street. One duelist wants witnesses and the other wants everyone gone.

name: A compass tuned to what was stolen

gm.title: At the table
lines: A compass points to a movable piece of iron. Documentary evidence says it was once calibrated against a fixed object that vanished.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A magician's cottage turns its doors away from the road whenever someone approaches quickly. A delivery person can model the greeting it recognizes.

name: A crab takes a small problem off the deck

gm.title: At the table
lines: The crab collects loose pegs and puts them in a box below the strongest nearby smell. A barrel owner swears the bilge plug was put back. Follow the crab to learn if the plug was removed or if the keeper is looking in the wrong compartment.

name: A credible compromise the villain refuses

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write down one exchange that would help both sides. Identify what keeps the opposition from taking it and give the party a way to change that condition.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A new field plant can ease pain, but it fruits only where a rare moth survives. The grain cooperative wants to plow the neighboring ditch.

name: A crown over a junk dealer's mark

gm.title: At the table
lines: A jeweled crown was plated over reused metal. A repair exposes part of a manufacturer's mark on the inside.

name: A crystal eye rides an empty boat

gm.title: At the table
lines: An artificial eye lies in the center of a skiff that stayed dry in an oily slick. Return it to its owner before the harbor sorts the boat as salvage, or trade the eye for an account of the slick.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Guests throw a battered cup through hoops. The cup always renews itself by dawn, but one new piece bears an unfamiliar maker's mark.

name: A cupboard hinge repeats whichever side opened it

gm.title: At the table
lines: A creature nesting in a hinge makes a rising sound when the door opened from inside and a falling sound otherwise. It repeats only when the kitchen is empty. The party can wait beyond the closed kitchen door to hear the last opening while the staff look for a missing tray.

name: A curious monster brings a replacement

gm.title: At the table
lines: A large sea creature takes anything dropped overboard and brings back something of similar shape. The next object it offers marks a channel the boat cannot enter at its current draft.

name: A curse leaves empty nails in familiar houses

gm.title: At the table
lines: Any drawing hung in a house on the affected block is found standing upright at the ruins of the old courthouse by dawn. Copies of the same drawing congregate there. An intact framed map can show which parcels still count as part of the block.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hex has shifted from shopkeeper to buyer. Both receipts give the buyer the right to a return, but every attempt to hand over the object shifts it again.

name: A dance beneath a quiet house

gm.title: At the table
lines: The upstairs owners enforce silence. Underground, dancers use steps to signal arrivals to someone posted in the alley.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A courtier refuses gifts because every past gift became a debt. Add one ally willing to help anonymously and one who needs public credit.

name: A deck pet marks who actually handled the crate

gm.title: At the table
lines: The ship's bird retrieves a polished peg when a familiar crate is unloaded and carries it to the person who removed the crate lid. Today it goes to the outgoing cook. Compare the cook’s account with the deck tally before assigning custody.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A dead investigator walks the same route seeking a witness who grew up and moved away. Find the witness under their adult name or show the ghost a later copy of the case.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A jewel reappears in the nearest tied purse whenever dropped. Search who packed the nearest tied container before the theft.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Residents begin changing shape whenever they trade coats at a particular stall. Pin down who wore each garment before the rain washes the labels away.

name: A dog guards an empty camp

gm.title: At the table
lines: A frightened dog defends a camp nobody has used for days. Returning the stray's missing collar settles it long enough to search.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every guest enters in costume. Someone wearing the same mask as a party member arrived hours ago and paid for two seats.

name: A dragon changes altitude to make shelter for another flyer

gm.title: At the table
lines: When a juvenile tries a crossing, an older dragon circles low to force a steady upward draft in the gorge. Travelers who know the routine can cross in its wake or get out of the narrow road before the second pass.

name: A dragon courts through visible acts of upkeep

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each spring two dragons compete to finish the largest useful local repair. One moved a rock to change a stream and left a mill without power. The rival is interested in finishing the neglected work if locals agree they can judge the result.

name: A dragon keeps its molted scales for repairs

gm.title: At the table
lines: Weathered breast scales naturally fall onto a stone shelf. The dragon arranges them by season and uses the tough layers to bridge leaks in its lair ceiling. It trades a loose scale only after someone shows where the leak can be patched without it.

name: A dragon’s roof has two built-in routes for rainfall

gm.title: At the table
lines: Outside one stream feeds a safe pool. A concealed gutter diverts the other stream around a bed of fragile crystals. Look for a dry seam to find the hidden gutter. Tilt the slab toward the seam to divert water away from the crystals, or put it on the exposed channel to flood the route behind your group.

name: A drifting fence reveals the salt road

gm.title: At the table
lines: Fence posts slide in shallow salt crust as the wind turns, but four buried feet keep their original line. Check which posts rock and follow the fixed ones to a hard surface before moving the wagon.

name: A dryad offers seed instead of coin

gm.title: At the table
lines: A grove keeper offers a seed that will grow wherever the party deposits it. Taking the reward means deciding who gets to tend what grows.

name: A faction's dues fund one person the members never meet

gm.title: At the table
lines: A line in the membership register pays an absent specialist from each applicant's first month's dues. Follow the payments to the person who maintains the public wards. They offer to keep doing the work if the party can arrange a public stipend. Decide whether to disclose their former source of support before the council votes.

name: A familiar body carries a new tool

gm.title: At the table
lines: The party recognizes a dead traveler whose tools belong to a different trade. A guild mark leads to where they learned that trade.

name: A familiar greeting ends when someone mentions the change

gm.title: At the table
lines: A contact greets the party as usual while hiding a problem. Decide which thing they hope nobody will mention and how their greeting breaks off when someone does. The players can ask privately or bring the issue into the room.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A trusted merchant misses market for the first time in years. A neighboring seller has been asked to cash an unusual set of receipts on their behalf.

name: A farm keeps one room aired

gm.title: At the table
lines: An abandoned farm has every entrance blocked except the pantry vent. A yearly festival still stores something there as part of an old agreement.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bright feather releases heat the first time each person takes it. It has already cooled for someone who claims never to have seen it.

name: A fey village elects its last visitor

gm.title: At the table
lines: When a newcomer arrives, the preceding visitor becomes mayor until they can hand over the sash. The older mayor has let the roads go unmarked to postpone that moment. Find out what unfinished promise they lose the power to fulfill upon leaving office.

name: A fissure separates the mule team

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tremor leaves pack animals on a ledge with just enough room to stand still. The cargo has to come off first.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A flask stays full even when poured. The same amount disappears from a marked cistern that many people rely on.

name: A flower sends back a memory

gm.title: At the table
lines: Sleep beside the bloom to recall one detail from a forgotten place. Ask which detail the character looks for and give one image they can verify awake.

name: A forecast needs a witness in both places

gm.title: At the table
lines: A diviner and a willing contact physically present at the destination each see the same ten seconds of one possible future there. Each glimpse shows the other witness’s face. Give the diviner a choice of contacts with different terms for participating.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A traveler sets out birthday cakes for guests who won't arrive. The empty seats are marked with places the party can check.

name: A foundation shelters the town it displaced

gm.title: At the table
lines: The bridge footings were built above an old cluster of rooms. Light a candle in one upper opening and people below knock in answer. Clearing the public path would expose both a settlement and the safe way across at flood stage.

name: A front door can borrow the builder's shadow

gm.title: At the table
lines: The carpenter who hung the door can step through once a day without opening it. Tomorrow they retire, and the house can transfer the privilege only while both carpenters are present. The old carpenter wants one hour inside to recover their own work before the handover.

name: A fugitive asks for neutral ground

gm.title: At the table
lines: A former servant wants shelter and insists their old employer is coming. The host needs a neutral witness to offer protection lawfully.

name: A gate ring carries paint from a distant shutter

gm.title: At the table
lines: A scrap of yellow paint is trapped between the old ring and its housing. It matches a chipped shutter at a second site where the gate stood last month. Find the carpenter who moved the whole gate and ask why its ownership marks were left behind.

name: A ghost ship wants its passengers discharged

gm.title: At the table
lines: A spectral captain cannot dock until someone ashore signs the passenger manifest. The harbor office finds two names that already belong to living citizens.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A house ghost lets one living visitor see where its friend used to sit. It will leave if somebody who knows that friend publicly acknowledges the friendship.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An iridescent scale drifts against the current when wet. Floating it at a fork can narrow the search for the animal that shed it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A masterless construct follows house numbers in order and stops at every missing number. The oldest town map shows why one address was removed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A lonely grave has an epitaph addressed to whoever comes after a particular date. A second inscription is visible when the light falls low.

name: A guarantee follows a doorway instead of a trade

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shop legend says all work done at the address must be repaired there. Recent renovations moved the door without moving the shop. Two owners claim the guarantee shifted. Let the party ask who can demonstrate an old repair before settling which claimant gets the next fee.

name: A halo moves like a lantern

gm.title: At the table
lines: A halo visibly lights the wall above a barricade while its wearer stays behind it. Make the light obvious before anyone attempts to hide.

name: A harmless guest in the hand

gm.title: At the table
lines: A small animal appears briefly wherever the drinker holds out cupped hands. A boy recognizes it as the same species that ruined his flower bed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Notes follow the drinker's voice and give away which words they emphasize. A bard can take down the pattern as a separate melody.

name: A healer asks where a mark was drawn

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two artists draw the same public decoration but place the small maker's dot on different edges. Their clients last week queued in different buildings. Find the booking list for the correct artist to learn who had contact with a missing person.

name: A hearth crab clicks for the table that feeds it

gm.title: At the table
lines: The crab patrols a tavern's hearthstone and retreats when strangers reach toward it. It accepts a saucer of brine and answers the knock pattern of the server that usually feeds it. Tonight someone in a private room knows that rhythm.

name: A heel print full of brick

gm.title: At the table
lines: A giant track contains shards from a kiln. The local masons can tell whether the giant came to rob them or happened to step in a collapsed wall.

name: A hill has a stair for every tax bracket

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each of three sets of stairs reaches the same tollhouse but was built under a different charter. The unused public stair can reopen if someone finds where a later landowner bricked up its lower arch.

name: A horned draft animal blocks the road

gm.title: At the table
lines: An armored wagon gives priority to its giant draft animal's rest. The traders will take detour advice if it reaches a place where the animal can turn around.

name: A hunter wants the correct culprit

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bounty hunter has a description that fits two people. They will split the reward for proof the one they caught is wrong.

name: A journeyman has tools from three closed shops

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each shop closed after the owner's legal address changed. The tools remain on three loan lists. They can be returned one by one or assembled to run the former shared workshop, with the borrowers choosing who keeps a key.

name: A knight wants a local cause

gm.title: At the table
lines: An eager knight asks about threats they can end before supper. The person doing the real work asks them to lend gear instead.

name: A large fish trails a line

gm.title: At the table
lines: A predator trails the vessel with a line caught on its fin. It only approaches when the ship slows. Cutting the line gives it a reason to leave and the party a marked hook to trace.

name: A lawn sinks where the new pitch says it should rise

gm.title: At the table
lines: The youngest groundskeeper can still reveal the former terrace line by rolling a ball downhill. A match roster is due tonight. Follow the line to the damaged drain or move a celebrated contest indoors and face the two clubs.

name: A letter of credit for a dead bank

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old letter can be redeemed at a bank nobody recalls. Paying out the value would restore the bank's charter and expose an existing debtor.

name: A letter sealed against its own opener

gm.title: At the table
lines: A purpose-made letter opener will slice anything except the envelope sold alongside it. Hold its edge to the stamp to reveal whose permission the seal requires.

name: A local legend has a different ending at each doorway

gm.title: At the table
lines: Shopkeepers tell visitors how the great fire stopped. Each knows the last thing they saw happen from their own doorway. Give the party two positions where the stories can both be right and a third where they can see what lay between.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A closed group keeps a new guest in a house with reinforced shutters. Neighbors hear the same toast every hour and know where the wine comes in.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A whirlpool opens a route to an underwater market at slack tide. The down-current entrance is safe only while a basalt marker is visible. The other route remains open but carries a toll.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A junk seller prices an enchanted object as everyday stock. An apprentice races to buy it back before their employer finds out.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bird takes bright badges and keys but ignores coin. Its nest holds tokens from every halted road crew. The watch will change the locks by dawn if its key is still missing.

name: A maker quotes two prices for the same mug

gm.title: At the table
lines: One price includes lifetime repairs by the maker. The lower price comes with the recipe for the glaze so another worker can repair it. If asked, the maker will name which other shop has the correct kiln.

name: A map drawn for the tide

gm.title: At the table
lines: A route ends at a point apparently empty on land. It makes sense only against a chart that shows low-water obstructions.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A chest opens for one passerby per hour. Its offerings provide exactly what a person needs to commit an act the market would condemn.

name: A midpoint that gives away leverage

gm.title: At the table
lines: Introduce a discovery that changes what people can ask for without dictating what the party should do. Let it reopen at least one route that looked closed in the first act.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Thousands of beetles travel in a straight line at dusk. Campers can pack up or learn which ordinary scent sends them around the tents.

name: A minute to see unseen guests

gm.title: At the table
lines: A drink reveals creatures using invisibility for a minute. An opaque barrier still hides whatever stands behind it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A desert inn only appears when a traveler gives up looking for it. A regular has left supplies outside the door for people who cannot bring themselves to stop.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Children disappear along one school route. A retired crossing guard remembers when the missing group started leaving a seat empty on purpose.

name: A missing tool turns up ahead

gm.title: At the table
lines: An object misplaced on the trail appears farther ahead already worn with use. A second object can be left behind to repeat the test.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Nobody remembers who kept the last watch. The mud records which boots went outside and which fire was burning.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A loose fence panel acts like an impassable border for a particular family. A land charter gives the terms under which it can be relocated.

name: A mute instrument knows the rhythm

gm.title: At the table
lines: An instrument plays silently but moves dust along the sounding board. One nearby musician can read the arrangement by watching the dust.

name: A naked runner and a uniform

gm.title: At the table
lines: Guards chase a streaker who refuses a cloak because it carries a stolen badge. The crowd thinks the badge belongs to the guard doing the chasing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An illegal fishing boat snared a merfolk messenger. Opening the holding tank will free the messenger and lose evidence of the catch. Find a way to preserve a witness, the ship's log, or the net before opening it.

name: A noble announces the wrong news

gm.title: At the table
lines: A public address reads an announcement meant for tomorrow. Copies posted at the city gates bear a different seal.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Treat a famine, disputed law, or migration as a force that changes people's choices. Put two people in charge of different responses and let players influence which response can spread.

name: A nose for an older visitor

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker distinguishes recent smells from older ones. Given an object that carries a reference scent, they can recognize it in a crowded room.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A preacher recruits in the market and includes a detail from a private conversation. A gap in the crowd provides a line of sight to the person feeding it to them.

name: A peddler who keeps asking directions

gm.title: At the table
lines: A persistent peddler names a different local landmark every time they approach. These are addresses being tested in front of someone who follows them.

name: A performer remembers the audience by seating

gm.title: At the table
lines: Their ledger records donated seats and working people who stood by the exit. Use the seating plan to distinguish two people with the same name, or ask the performer which scene prompted an early departure.

name: A permit is valid only in its issuing voice

gm.title: At the table
lines: A clerk's permit was spoken in a way the ward recognizes. Their apprentice can repeat it if someone finds the record of the original recipients. The gate is still willing to admit a visitor who can make a case for a fresh permit.

name: A pillar points to a second door

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fixed magical light sends a pillar's shadow across the floor. Rotating the pillar makes the shadow line up with worn outlines of doors on different walls, opening one at a time. One outline remains open while the party tests the others.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A long coat's pockets accept many objects but come up empty unless searched in the original order. Seams reveal how many items someone left.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A harmless small storm appears over the drinker. Raising a copper rod makes it flash and can signal across a dark courtyard.

name: A pool records which way the guardian walked

gm.title: At the table
lines: When the guardian moves, its weight tilts the mineral floor slightly. Look for wall marks exposed by the falling end of the pool. They show which side has tipped and which passage remains above water.

name: A portrait follows only a thief

gm.title: At the table
lines: Several visitors think the eyes of a portrait follow them. Test a wall hook from the portrait's old room to establish exactly when its gaze shifts.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A woodworker asks travelers to sit while they carve a likeness. The figures taken from the previous sitting include a person nobody saw on the trail.

name: A potter's sample break shows where the heat was

gm.title: At the table
lines: A judge has two clay fragments from the failed repair. The potter can match the scorch boundary to the side that was still against the stove wall. Refit the pieces to see whether the pot broke in the kitchen or was heated after removal.

name: A prisoner asks for a witness

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shackled prisoner calls out details of a contract still posted on a wall. The notice names a surety who can intervene before the prisoner crosses the bridge into the next jurisdiction. Find the surety or invoke the clause in public.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fruit of gold must be given to the sculpture marked as judge. The central seat is empty, but the verdict lies beneath the feet of one figure. Find which figure was meant to judge the others, or reconstruct the same solution from an account in a side room.

name: A procession carries the wrong coat on purpose

gm.title: At the table
lines: The clothing of a past officeholder leads the celebration. This year workers carry their predecessor's everyday coat instead of their official robes. The two families involved have a reason to honor different versions of the same service.

name: A public wall keeps an open account

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every block added to a shared wall is recorded in a numbered register. An unnumbered course is holding back the city's dry-season stream. Identify the builder and put an emergency repair on record without settling the full property claim.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Coins spilled in a gutter match the sum posted as a ransom. Carrying them to the watch alerts whoever is checking the gutter.

name: A quill fits a borrowed signature

gm.title: At the table
lines: A pen changes the user's handwriting. The stable ink color can prove which contradictory letters were written on the same day.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A raven shifts leaves along the edge of a monster print. Its handler will trade information only if the party lets the method remain secret.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Place a person or object in a contested spot. When the party reaches it, change how both sides move so extraction has its own choices.

name: A reflection remembers where things belong

gm.title: At the table
lines: Several objects in a mirror sit in places that differ from the room. Their real positions have dust outlines. Recreate the positions seen in the mirror to unlatch a passage, or open it from the far side through a service corridor.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A seasick passenger is hiding in the hold. Telling the captain earned the last stowaway an unwanted return home. Finding a person on the roster willing to vouch can make the stowaway a paying guest.

name: A refuse creature keeps a clean shelf

gm.title: At the table
lines: It stores shiny objects outside its feeding pit on a dry shelf. Leave it a choice of scrap and food and it will exchange one object at a time. The last traveler paid with the item the party wants and might return with a better offer.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Water empties through a slit in the air. Across it someone is building a dam with the stones that have disappeared from the pasture wall.

name: A repair artist finishes from the other end

gm.title: At the table
lines: A damaged moving line can be redrawn from either of two ends. Restoring it from the wrist preserves who set it last, and restoring it from the elbow restores its earlier trigger. Let the player ask who can document each option.

name: A repair asks for the old form back after sunset

gm.title: At the table
lines: The spell restores an object until dusk, when its owner has to undo one chosen reversible alteration to it. Let the caster identify acceptable alterations first, such as a moved handle or newly painted edge, and buy the owner time to decide.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An accident snaps an object the party relied on. The only maker who can mend it wants the wreck returned intact to establish its provenance.

name: A rescue guild requires bad news in pairs

gm.title: At the table
lines: The guild refuses to tell a family of a death unless two witnesses can attend together. One witness will enter only through a side door. A party member who recovered a personal effect from the scene qualifies as a second witness. The group can accompany the available witness, arrange the closed meeting, or ask the guild to make an exception.

name: A rescuer might acquire an empty estate

gm.title: At the table
lines: A town has a rule that the person who recovers a family deed from an inundated archive gains temporary control of the property. Name who still lives there and give the party an option to transfer custody before they retrieve it.

name: A retired wizard suggests a route

gm.title: At the table
lines: A helpful wizard can chart their former stronghold in detail but remembers different reasons for sealing its rooms. Let the party compare their testimony with the letters they wrote before leaving.

name: A returned delivery earns half pay and one answer

gm.title: At the table
lines: The hiring notice pays full for delivery. After seeing the destination has been abandoned, players may bring the parcel back sealed for half and learn why it keeps being sent, or find the intended recipient.

name: A ribbon ties a knot in another room

gm.title: At the table
lines: A ribbon's knot cannot be reached from either end. Two people holding different ends can trace the path of its missing loop with chalk on opposite walls.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Street fighting breaks out around the square. Sellers have already opened a chain of adjoining yards to help people move without crossing it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every evening an audible rhythm arrives upstream. Boats start grounding between beats. The ferrymen can restore the usual rhythm by opening a jammed gate before the evening crossing.

name: A road borrows three inches from each repaired wall

gm.title: At the table
lines: Fresh mortar creates an equal gap at the far edge of the road. Mark the change with a survey line, then decide whether to repair the wall this week or close the road while a new route is set out.

name: A rot crosses old parish lines

gm.title: At the table
lines: An unnatural rot follows obsolete religious borders. The people outside those borders can help choose where to quarantine and which old boundary markers to restore.

name: A route stays open while a floor turns

gm.title: At the table
lines: Lay out two rings with visible exits. Moving the inner ring closes one path and opens another. Show the alignment marks in a handout and let a character hold one ring still while the rest move.

name: A runaway goat drags a cord

gm.title: At the table
lines: A goat broke out of a pen with a line of handwritten tags still tied to its collar. Each tag marks an animal being moved that night.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A ball displays rooms with all their lights out. The party can steady a view by asking a willing contact to shutter one window at a time.

name: A sea god asks for ordinary labor

gm.title: At the table
lines: A divine messenger asks the party to move a milestone that marks an old fishing ground. Ask neighboring crews who expects to gain access if the line moves.

gm.title: At the table
lines: This seed opens overnight after a day in direct light. A scout can use its glow as a signal or hide it before the watch passes.

name: A seed cloud at ankle height

gm.title: At the table
lines: A marsh plant releases its seeds at sunset and the haze stays low. A local directs small travelers to platforms at the edge until it settles.

name: A serpent that trusts only starlight

gm.title: At the table
lines: A large nocturnal snake refuses to cross a patch lit by torches. Its nest is on a rock that will submerge at sunrise, giving the party a chance to guide it instead of fighting.

name: A shadow the color of cloth

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker's shadow changes to a bright solid hue, making it easy to distinguish at the edge of torchlight.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The shadow runs ahead of the drinker without leaving their side. It flinches back if someone beyond the corner sees it, giving the drinker time to stop.

name: A shell game against the clock

gm.title: At the table
lines: A street game stalls customers while a lookout waits for a delivery. Once the delivery passes, the dealer wants help recovering a legitimately lost token.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A royal seal authorizes a mundane repair. Its custodian swears it has been locked away since a previous reign.

name: A single stair and many floors

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every landing offers a louder band than the one below. Only a visitor closing both ears hears a hand knocking from the sealed halfway floor.

name: A sitter the sculptor can't name

gm.title: At the table
lines: A statue shows unfamiliar proportions and carries a local artist's mark. The maker remembers the measurements but no parts of the sitting.

name: A skull opens one eye at midnight

gm.title: At the table
lines: At midnight the light in one eye turns toward the place where the skull was last deliberately buried. There is a short window to take a bearing before it closes.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Symbols cut on a skull label places its owner never visited. The knife marks set some labels years apart.

name: A slime trail with dry edges

gm.title: At the table
lines: A trail stays wet in the middle while its edges dry. Watch the wet center contract toward a wall crack. Blocking the crack makes the trail slacken and gives a glimpse of the thing pulling it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The same melody makes different residents walk to different thresholds. It falters when someone sings the part missing from the town's festival version.

name: A spell spends a right of way

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shortcut opens by consuming temporary access to one ordinary route the caster was authorized to use. Display both affected thresholds before the spell completes. The lost access returns after the caster visibly takes the longer way once.

name: A spillway has two legal fishing sides

gm.title: At the table
lines: The shore lease grants one bank the right to take fish approaching the fall. The other bank can take fish going back downstream. Hand-copied maps disagree on the middle pool. The keeper will let the party survey it while both groups stand behind their own marker.

name: A spool proves where a parcel stopped

gm.title: At the table
lines: Unusually strong thin wire survives a shipment across a rough pass. It ends in a telltale repair knot used at only one depot. The depot's manifest names the person who brought a shorter spool back.

name: A spring's guardian tests its own seal

gm.title: At the table
lines: Three parties present letters granting permission to draw water. Its horn guard leaves a different wax mark for each approved request. The mark for winter watering appears on a letter promising daily access. Ask for the guard impressions to learn which approval someone copied.

name: A square is a reservoir after sundown

gm.title: At the table
lines: Channels fill a paved square each evening. A fixture recessed in the paving is reachable while it is dry. The district can postpone the day's filling for a fee, but decide who receives the water first if the delay spills into the next day.

name: A stall's free samples introduce the customers

gm.title: At the table
lines: The owner asks visitors to taste two batches and say which stall really made each one. Customers know the local supplier by seasoning. A merchant nearby has been mislabeling wares and is willing to settle before an inspector tastes them.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A herd is pushed toward a ravine by weather. Fence builders ask the party to open a barrier that would divert it into valuable crops.

name: A statue that is warm at the joints

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stone figure takes a single breath when rain begins. Ask the party what would convince them to carry it out of the storm.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A messenger carries an unsigned stay of judgment. The judge can still be found if someone can get past the audience.

name: A stolen portrait is still in outline

gm.title: At the table
lines: The Memory soot lantern beside an empty easel shows the silhouette of a frame blocking its light. One witness claims the frame was boxed first. Test which of two storage boxes would leave that outline, then decide whether to follow the matching crate or track the unboxed portrait.

name: A stone falls out of a cloud

gm.title: At the table
lines: A warm stone strikes the trail and sinks into dirt. The imprint reveals it was set in a larger frame before it fell.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The ale counter is at the top of a climbing wall. A bartender uses the rest ledge halfway up for talks nobody on either end should hear.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Sparks attach to old copper fittings and let them hold voices for an hour. The watch wants every fitting collected before anyone hears its orders.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An apparent charm makes a stranger sound painfully familiar. The details they know are real, and the source wants them traced.

name: A street dog enforces a route

gm.title: At the table
lines: A dog blocks travel through one alley and offers no trouble elsewhere. The collar has delivery times scratched inside.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The fire skips three houses on a windy street. Residents want quick passage back inside and the firefighters want the houses searched first.

name: A supplier honors the buyer's labor

gm.title: At the table
lines: Let a merchant offer a lower fitting charge if the customer has already found the missing measurement, brought a sample of the old part, or cleaned the piece. State the normal price first so the decision is visible.

name: A sword that rejects an edge

gm.title: At the table
lines: A blunt sword sheds any edge ground into it. Its owner's contracts treat it as a tool for dubbing, which makes the edge itself a claim to office.

name: A tab moth eats unpaid ink

gm.title: At the table
lines: A moth settles on the newest unpaid line of the innkeeper's ledger. Blank paper will distract it long enough to copy a name, but sweet fruit gets it to leave the book entirely.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hare knows the hunters' words and repeats them only from inside a burrow. Once it trusts a listener it names which claim it wants verified.

name: A tattoo moves only in a repeated pose

gm.title: At the table
lines: The ink sits differently when the bearer returns to their posture at its application. Let the player test several positions. The revealed shape can be a hand signal, an identifying mark, or one part of a map the artist drew while asking the subject to hold still.

name: A tattooist will show a tracing first

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the player a washable sample and name the exact condition that activates the permanent mark. Ask which part they want visible under ordinary clothes and how to show that feature during play.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The inn sails to a different quay after the last order. A witness will board only if the party can guarantee a landing in neutral waters.

name: A test piece is worth more to an apprentice

gm.title: At the table
lines: The finished item is ready, but an apprentice wants one draft or offcut returned to show how they learned. Give the player a lower price for transferring the test piece, a choice of another sample, and one way to get permission to keep both.

name: A thaw moves the ford after noon

gm.title: At the table
lines: Morning cart tracks cross safely. By afternoon meltwater deposits sand on the paved ford and cuts back one bank. A painted post shows the last hour a loaded cart can safely cross, and a footbridge remains open upriver.

name: A threshold that can't match daylight

gm.title: At the table
lines: A portal offers open air and a midday sun long after dusk. Tossing through string shows the ground beyond lies at a steep angle.

name: A tincture for the wrong thing

gm.title: At the table
lines: A crowd buys a merchant's relief tonic. The only customer demanding a refund expected it to keep a magical light from going out.

name: A tiny wick asks to see the child it lit

gm.title: At the table
lines: A living wick remembers a tune sung beside its lamp. It can tap the rhythm when it hears the lamp’s cracked shutter. Play the tune at the house where the lamp came from to find a former neighbor who helped the child’s family leave.

name: A token buys bad luck on credit

gm.title: At the table
lines: Anyone who accepts a particular faerie coin as payment finds an unpaid bill later in the week. The bill always bears the same merchant's stamp regardless of the purchase.

name: A tower rents one floor to a different school every day

gm.title: At the table
lines: Shifts share tools stored in the same layout with different meanings for their tags. An apprentice can show yesterday's arrangement if the party helps reset the rooms before the next leaseholder arrives.

name: A town too happy to stop

gm.title: At the table
lines: A sudden wave of euphoria keeps workers from noticing danger. Anyone who leaves the square notices that the mood fades on the far side of an old drain.

name: A trader sells honest seconds with a label

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stall sells old hardware and states one obvious flaw on each tag. Give buyers an easy way to tell whether that flaw matters for their intended use. If a second, hidden problem turns up, the seller offers to buy the broken part for anything they can recover from it.

name: A trapdoor opens under its own shadow

gm.title: At the table
lines: A loose hatch has a small empty space behind it, wherever it is laid. A person confined inside can reach out only while someone stands across its shadow.

name: A tree house rocks in still air

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hermit says the house rocks whenever a creature climbs the roots below. One root is hollow and worth listening to.

name: A tree splits to reveal writing

gm.title: At the table
lines: Lightning opens a tree and exposes carving made while it was young. One name matches a present-day family who interpret it differently.

name: A unicorn offers to escort only one of two caravans

gm.title: At the table
lines: It knows a safe route but won't leave the grove unguarded for long. The caravan carrying injured strangers can take the first crossing if the other drivers agree to watch the approach. The party can take either job or arrange an exchange at the midpoint.

name: A village cobbler keeps three valid endings to a journey

gm.title: At the table
lines: Mending a visitor’s soles settles one debt tied to their last journey. The cobbler can record an unpaid toll as waived, release a formal hospitality obligation, or certify a failed delivery attempt. The party chooses which cost or obligation they want discharged.

name: A visitor with the wrong season

gm.title: At the table
lines: A trader from far away insists their delegation walked through snow that morning. Their luggage is full of summer plants wrapped for transport.

name: A voice from an uncertain corner

gm.title: At the table
lines: A drink makes whispers difficult to locate in a room. An ally who sees the speaker's mouth can still pick them out.

name: A waking guide leaves chalk lines in only one dream house

gm.title: At the table
lines: Walk the waking neighborhood to learn where the guide has actually been. Inside the dream neighborhood the chalk follows one recognizable threshold to a house owned by someone else. Put an honest message there and wait to see who can carry it back.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A round scorch mark holds heat only inside the ring. Tracks go right up to the edge and continue on the underside of the mine roof.

name: A warning signed by a dead guide

gm.title: At the table
lines: A message orders travelers off the road using a dead guide's signature. Their apprentice can show which route was meant and why the signature was used.

name: A watering place shared by rivals

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two herds arrive at one pool. A traveler can move a trough to separate them if the landowner agrees to spare water.

name: A well works only for the household downhill

gm.title: At the table
lines: Lowering a bucket makes a counterweight lift a plug in a second well. Both households can draw in turn so long as neither tries to fit a permanent pump. The party arrives with a pump that could settle one shortage and start another.

name: A window drake rehearses the household routine

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drake perches outside when the shutters open and mimics everyday gestures in miniature. A caller claims the house was empty last week. Offer a warm ledge and the drake repeats a familiar greeting from that week at the exact shutter it was taught to visit.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bystander insists they caused a mishap the party saw. They are trying to draw attention away from who was in the crowd.

name: A witness with a blind spot

gm.title: At the table
lines: An otherwise reliable mapmaker omits every place where they broke an oath. A mundane survey gives the party something to compare.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A suspected werewolf hunts at night. A laundress can show which customer orders emergency clothes at dawn and tries to pay in advance.

name: A wolf waits for the pack

gm.title: At the table
lines: One wolf blocks the road but glances repeatedly uphill. The rest are carrying pups across a stretch exposed to travelers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A lost traveler swears they followed every marker in order. Their boots carry evidence from the path the patrol has quietly diverted traffic onto. Find out what the patrol is keeping traders away from.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A self-appointed investigator serves identical charges on rival spellcasters. Both warrants come from the same sheet, with spaces left for the names.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A returning group offers a recovered object for the party's ordinary rope. The rope is needed to make the rest of their promised rescue.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A transparent shell preserves an injured scout. One side has thinned enough to speak through and the scout can direct rescue.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A calculating frame is accurate in most hands. With the accounts of one official, it consistently omits a single levy.

name: An alley is listed under a different owner every morning

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old boundary charter assigns use of a gate to whoever sweeps the alley before sunrise. Merchants trade favors for turns. The night the party needs it, two brooms lean against the lock.

name: An ally is upset about a task you finished too well

gm.title: At the table
lines: The party solved a nuisance completely. An ally who got reliable work maintaining the partial fix asks them to introduce the ally to people who still need that skill. State what the ally valued about the old work before asking for help.

name: An ally walks the other way

gm.title: At the table
lines: A trusted friend passes on the trail with no time to stop and slips a bundle into someone's hands. Check its contents before following.

name: An animal has one minute to explain

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker can speak with nearby animals briefly. Let one animal describe what it sensed without identifying people or places it has never learned.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A young adventurer copies the group's mannerisms and gets mistaken for its emissary. A shopkeeper accepted their promise as payment.

name: An eclipse with one bright pane

gm.title: At the table
lines: A street goes dark early except for one sunlit window. Evidence in the room suggests the light is waiting for someone who missed a meeting.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old siege engine stuck in mud blocks travelers under its own weight. A descendant of the crew will explain its concealed cargo before the party moves it.

name: An entertainer has a request they always refuse

gm.title: At the table
lines: Pick a piece with a local association and a specific person who dislikes it. A patron calls for it in front of them. Show whether the entertainer declines by words, by changing the tune, or by leaving the stage.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each turn takes a different time depending on who is watching it. Measure the difference when one person leaves the room.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stew pot refills whenever its last portion is served. The only way to change what comes back is to feed the first bowl to whoever cooked the original batch.

name: An injured animal keeps getting up

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wounded boar drags itself toward a creek. Its old snare is clean enough to trace to a nearby trapper.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stamp takes on a new shape after every use. A sheaf of impressions can establish which papers were made before a disputed transfer.

name: An odd job comes with a shared deadline

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two clients need the same piece of public equipment during one short working window. State what each job earns, what favor matters more than money, and one way the parties could split the time.

name: An ogre feast makes the kitchen a neutral room

gm.title: At the table
lines: Guests refuse to negotiate in the main hall, where seating confers rank. The cooks run a private negotiation over a bowl of vegetables to peel. One delegation offers grain if the bridge toll is waived. The other can lend guards to keep the bridge open on market days. A courtier outside would like to know why the cooks have so many volunteers.

name: An otyugh describes rubbish by the route it took

gm.title: At the table
lines: The creature tastes the trace of each chute mixed in a heap. Offer a sample from a known chute and it can identify which public building a torn letter came from. A building with two refuse routes gives two possible rooms to check.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Across a narrow gully, cast spells produce an echo at the caster's old position. Pebbles with simple charms let the group test the boundary.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Families hear ancestral voices through the festival drums. Two voices dispute the same inheritance and can each answer one question.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Livestock scatter through the streets in the same order every afternoon. A driver can observe which street noise starts the stampede.

name: Ask for the result before the method

gm.title: At the table
lines: Before resolving an unusual action, ask what the player wants to be true afterward. If their proposed method would accomplish something else, explain the difference before they commit. An apparently bad tactic may be a good answer to a goal the table had missed.

name: Ask what repair would actually settle the debt

gm.title: At the table
lines: A player chooses a past mistake they want to revisit and describes what the harmed person lost. Offer two possible forms of repair with separate costs. Ask the player what would signify that the matter was settled.

name: Ask what the NPC knows from doing the work

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give each local specialist one clue they can demonstrate using their trade. They can disagree with someone else's interpretation while showing the party what they actually observed.

name: Ask which promise two people remember differently

gm.title: At the table
lines: Have the player write their character's wording and name the other person. Ask permission to supply the other wording before drafting. The two versions should support different legitimate expectations when they surface in play.

name: Ask who never returned a borrowed implement

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the group a loan shelf at a recurring inn or community hall. The host will replace a missing tool if the party delivers a note to the last borrower; the same entry can lead to someone the players already wanted to meet.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A crew asks if a protected wagon already passed. They will reconsider their plan if shown whose goods it is actually carrying.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker hovers the width of a finger above flat ground. Place loose powder at the edge of a safe patch to show where solid support matters again.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fey can hold perfectly still against a trunk. Show twigs moving at shoulder height before revealing the sentinel and let a traveler offer news of a threatened grove.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Motion sets a soft chime ringing. Walking slowly changes the gaps between notes and permits a simple signal.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The visible veins of the drinker glow. A healer who follows the light can identify a tight bandage before removing it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Floodwater turns a bridge approach into an island. The infirmary needs a supply boat and a wealthy neighbor insists on the last available oars.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The river carries bodies at regular distances. Logging the intervals helps locate the narrow channel that periodically releases them.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An abandoned pair of boots is tidy and warm. Next to them are prints of bare feet walking into a place nobody would enter in winter.

name: Borrow the key by breaking eye contact

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stone guardian and a visitor seem to be staring at each other. Cover the line between their eyes and the visitor briefly thaws, key and all. They will lend it for a promise to hold the barrier up a little longer.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cellar maze shelves wine as it ages. Two passages look identical until a guest reads the vintage that hasn't happened yet.

gm.title: At the table
lines: For one minute the drinker can speak only to one person's mind at a time. The listener can always ignore it or answer aloud.

name: Bring in the fish or learn why the line went still

gm.title: At the table
lines: When a line stops moving, the player can reel in now, feed line out to follow the fish, or stop and map the sudden change in depth. Decide before the roll which rewards travel with the fish and which describe the place.

name: Broker a pause with two witnesses

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each side needs somebody who will guarantee a pause lasts. Put a reliable witness near each group and make the initial success a short truce the players can extend.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Everything in the inn is patched with the same cloth. An attentive guest can assemble parts of the old signal flag from the patches.

name: Build pressure from a specific loss

gm.title: At the table
lines: Choose a person, resource, or place a character has invested in. Show a reversible consequence early and a harder consequence later if the situation continues.

name: Build room for a quieter scene

gm.title: At the table
lines: After a high-pressure choice, place a witness, ally, or ordinary task the players can visit on their own terms. Use it to let them decide what the choice meant.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Candles measure the time their owners have left on a contract. One flame is eating through wax fast enough to make negotiation urgent.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A ship burns without drifting. A rope leading underwater keeps it beside a salvage crew retrieving a waterlogged chest. The crew asks for help keeping their air line out of the fire.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Birds circle low over a mound but pull up before landing. Wind around the mound carries one clear warning sound.

name: Carved marks face the deer trail

gm.title: At the table
lines: The rock's signs face a narrow animal track. A hunter recognizes them as a route marker meant for something shorter than a traveler.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Skin moves through bright colors even when the drinker stands still. The drinker can hold their breath to pause on a color and send a signal across the square.

name: Choose which faction detail only members can correct

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the public one broadly accurate story and one important mistaken detail. Introduce a lower-ranking member who can correct the detail if asked about a specific incident. Change what someone can negotiate once that correction becomes public.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Parallel gouges run along a bar from the courtyard side. Prove the gate was breached by an animal someone let in.

name: Compare a claimed catch against the known run

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fisher offers good money for claiming today's early catch as theirs. A buyer can identify the run from marks on the fish’s side and date it with a landing tally, which records who checked in before sunrise. Offer the party a reason to need the buyer's trust next week.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give a character's ally a sincere goal that conflicts with a promise the party depends on. Write an action the ally might take if left alone and what could convince them otherwise.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Bad copies of coins are traded in great quantity. The wrong side always bears a grain measure, so the copies let people settle a debt in goods.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A curfew starts at a bell nobody can hear in the mills. The guard sets up signals after the party proves who is missing it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The tavern is kept dark for a proprietor who can't bear a direct gaze. Someone has started selling smoked lenses that fail halfway through a shift.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Figures dance in the harvested field without bending a stalk. Their steps mark buried boundary stones that two farms claim.

name: Decide what they do with an idle hand

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the NPC one work habit that occupies a hand in normal conversation. When a subject interrupts that movement, let interested players ask why instead of requiring a check.

name: Decide where a rescued animal sleeps

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hungry animal follows the party to camp. Give it two possible shelters with different owners or risks. An evening spent observing how it behaves around each option helps the players place it without adopting it indefinitely.

name: Defeat the authority holding a truce

gm.title: At the table
lines: One enemy gives others orders through a recognized signal. Remove their ability to issue it or give a credible replacement signal to stop the fight before every combatant falls.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Casting bones always land on the same result for whoever owns them. Let two players test who the bones currently recognize.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cook lets anyone wager for food. The server quietly swaps the stakes for people they recognize from the same company.

name: Distribute the work without agreeing on the credit

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ask each partner which part of a joint mission they insist on doing. Let the public tally determine which partner qualifies to lead the next job. When both claim the same contribution, players can negotiate an account that names each role or save evidence that could change the decision later.

name: Draw one rule a defector still follows

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write one instruction a member will abandon when they leave and one promise they will honor afterward. Give both a visible test. An interested player can verify the defector's continuing responsibility without agreeing to trust them on everything.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two sleepers dream of today's camp one valley over. The slope in the dream reveals a safe route out if the weather turns.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two aquatic peoples answer in song. One echoes words to guide boats toward shore while the other repeats a loved one's voice to turn them toward rocks. Put both songs within earshot of a beacon.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Visible sparks shed from the drinker without burning. They can test an air current but also betray a hiding place.

gm.title: At the table
lines: New checkpoint rules stop cargo before they stop passengers. The fishmongers ask the party to move a day's stock by hand.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A repair invoice predates the damage it describes. Put two independent dates in play so the party can test whether time moved or someone forged the receipt.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Only a current member can sponsor a guest. Give each willing sponsor a different condition and a consequence for backing the party.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker's gaze casts a narrow beam. Covering the eyes extinguishes it and makes ordinary sight unavailable.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Portraits appear on the shell of a predator after every encounter. One face belongs to a living witness who insists that the others can still be recovered.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An empty cottage shows years of earnest repairs around a single collapsed wall. A bill nailed inside identifies the landowner still collecting rent.

gm.title: At the table
lines: If a bribe fails, the guard names the officer who can issue a permit. The group still has to decide whether to petition, wait, or risk a different entrance.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A local hero takes one visible risk too many and children begin imitating them. Give the hero a second way to earn their admiration.

name: Find a second source while someone repairs your gear

gm.title: At the table
lines: A repair takes one watch. Before paying for faster service, a player can spend that watch asking a trade witness a question tied to wear, stains, or local craft marks on the thing being repaired.

name: Find the skill a relationship depends on

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ask who taught the character something that still matters in play. Give the teacher a present-day problem with two viable ways to help, one using that skill and one requiring a new approach.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A forest fire approaches faster on one ridge than expected. Two crews can build only one firebreak before the wind changes.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Little silver fish swim over a flooded floor. They flee whenever a patron carrying a submerged object comes inside.

name: Fishing poles mark last spring’s safe ice

gm.title: At the table
lines: Painted poles mark where fishing holes were dug along a survey line last spring. The gaps indicate then-unsafe ice. This year a new pole beyond the old bend marks a hole directly above a submerged sluice.

name: Flailfish taste a changed current before other creatures feel it

gm.title: At the table
lines: They swim with their whiskers held to one side whenever a strong channel starts drawing water down. Suspend a perforated fish basket in each branch of an intake channel. Watch which way the fish turn once the baskets settle to tell which branch still flows.

gm.title: At the table
lines: One species flowers briefly when its night pollinators touch it. An empty field of closed blossoms signals that something interrupted the insects' route. The first open flowers point toward a new roost. Pollinating a patch by hand preserves the harvest and buys time to find out what moved the insects.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A school of small fish lands harmlessly aboard but blocks the openings that drain the deck. Clear them now or save the mess until after the captain notices the following squall.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fog shows the last people to stand on a patch of ground during an old disaster. Clearing the fog would help rescuers and destroy the evidence. Indoors, fresh limewash can hold the same image until a blocked window has to be broken.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Fresh fruit turns up beyond the range where it grows. A seller wants proof that the seeds will germinate before they pay its unexpected carrier.

name: Get a copy without catching the witness

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fleeing witness carries a document. Players can follow the street route and keep sight of them, or reach the nearer gate first and ask the watch to copy anything the witness voluntarily shows. Agree what counts as success even if nobody is caught.

name: Get through before the second sweep

gm.title: At the table
lines: Place a hazard between the group and somewhere they need to reach. Show the pattern of its return so the players can decide whether to time it or change the route.

name: Give a backstory keepsake two practical roles

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ask what it proves to someone from the character's old life and what it can do for a stranger who knows none of that history. Let the player decide which use they will show first.

name: Give a dormant thread a changed invitation

gm.title: At the table
lines: Set an unused lead aside until an NPC could take a further step. The next invitation says exactly what changed and why they are asking again. If the party declines, describe the action the NPC can take without them.

name: Give a faction a service worth preserving

gm.title: At the table
lines: Decide which routine service gives a faction public goodwill. Introduce it while it works. If the party opposes the faction, give it two viable operators with different obligations, so ending the faction need not end the service.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Decide who uses a person's nickname and one person who pointedly uses their formal title. During a scene, change the form of address only when the relationship changes or someone overhears it.

name: Give a red herring a fact worth following anyway

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the misleading clue a true explanation and an independent sign that excludes it from the main incident. Following it can help another person, remove a suspect, or turn up a witness without undoing the original clue.

name: Give each coalition partner a different deadline

gm.title: At the table
lines: Set one common goal and give each partner a specific last moment to act. Put at least two deadlines on the table before asking for a commitment. A party that cannot help both can still negotiate a delay or offer a narrower promise.

name: Give each fork a different problem

gm.title: At the table
lines: Describe two ways forward using the same distance unit. Put a known labor cost on one and an uncertain social cost on the other. Let a scout learn one detail about the uncertain cost before the group commits.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The arena's favorite asks the party to hold their place in line at a civic hearing while they finish a bout.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An alchemist's window blows outward and a bright liquid enters the gutter. The apprentice begs for the ledger before anyone asks why the vats were full.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Opaque glasses bear traces of a series of spoken testimony in the arms. The case carries two versions of one testimony and identifies neither as final.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A sneeze gives away the drinker in lamplight. A coat worn by the same person later retains a little glitter inside its sleeve.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A sexton leaves valuable possessions alone while opening specific graves. Counting the empty coffins points to the one burial they are trying to move.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The dead rise where prayers are still addressed to a god who has died. One family can describe a deceased person who never received the same rites.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A plant grows where a mourner wept. Carrying it helps someone speak the words they could not say at the funeral, then the plant withers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: In a rain-filled street, a small ray feeds along drains and changes direction at every pulse of runoff. Watching where it turns can reveal a blocked culvert. Clearing the blockage draws the ray away from a crowded stair, but may send water toward whatever lies beneath it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker's hair grows long enough to catch in buckles. The change ends at dawn, which gives a tail a reliable mark for the evening.

name: Hand the next decision to someone outside the exchange

gm.title: At the table
lines: When a long exchange resolves, give the next actionable question to a player who was listening. Ask who they want nearby or what cost they think the group should accept. Join the answer to the scene already in progress so their choice matters immediately.

gm.title: At the table
lines: These shell-backed grazers cling to railings and rasp away old paint. Their tracks expose earlier paint in the order the animals moved. A dab of mineral paste can guide them along a sealed landing, uncovering its original route marker while leaving the rest of the paint intact.

gm.title: At the table
lines: For a few minutes the drinker's palms glow. They can shut their fists to hide it, at the cost of putting down tools.

name: Horns that signal the wrong rank

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker grows a pair of tiny horns for ten minutes. Locals mistake their angle for membership in a club that owes the party an answer.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A continuous hum can steady a frightened animal willing to listen. The drinker has to stay nearby and leave the creature a path to retreat.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Night hunters cast flour across alleys to track something nobody else can see. The quarry's prints stop at a crowded shelter.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Rain falls inside the inn on cloudless days. The ceiling clears over a table reserved by a guest the staff haven't seen in weeks.

name: Ink that turns up on the reader

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ink is invisible on paper but stains the hands of whoever last held the sheet. A shared handwashing bowl can preserve both traces.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tavern has a dragon's jaw as its porch. A recent tooth has been fitted among old ones and the hunters disagree about where it came from.

name: Interrupt one link in the sequence

gm.title: At the table
lines: Tell players what they can see about a developing ceremony or public event. Identify at least two different links they could interrupt and show what each evening looks like if it breaks there.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A young diviner sees four hands holding a rope above a well. The view cuts off whenever one hand lets go, so eyewitness accounts of local rigging become important.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An apprentice withholds a patron's letter because it praises their colleague. Keep a dated entry in the messenger's book.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Make the table ruling for this scene and record the exact trigger in your notes. Revisit it between games.

name: Lantern fish show where the harbor mouth narrowed

gm.title: At the table
lines: The night shoal arrives at the old harbor line and turns where a wedge of fresh water splits the current. The bend puts a stranded boat behind a sand ridge its crew cannot see. Follow the school or send a shallow craft to sound the new approach.

name: Lantern makers leave one dark window

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each shop hangs a lamp to say it's ready to open after winter. A window stays dark because the owner's successor can only renew the license in person. Give the party one way to find them and one way to ask the market to keep the stall open meanwhile.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every table is catalogued with the book last borrowed there. A missing ledger can be traced through stains on the spine beside it.

name: Let a boundary end one role in a relationship

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give an ally and an opponent a narrow area where they still trust each other. When one crosses a clearly stated boundary, the trusted role ends. Their practical ties and any other agreements remain visible in the next scene.

name: Let a witness keep their reason for staying

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write one thing a witness fears and one concrete reason they have stayed nearby despite it. A safe escort can address the first. Helping their dependents or protecting their livelihood addresses the second. A convincing plan earns cooperation even if they never agree to leave.

name: Let an unresolved question acquire a keeper

gm.title: At the table
lines: Close the current arc by deciding who holds its outstanding mystery. The party can entrust a named steward, leave evidence in public, or keep the question for later. Add one way for a future patron to take an interest in it.

name: Let exploration leave a useful mark

gm.title: At the table
lines: When someone spends a watch mapping a hazardous stretch, give them one fact they can hand to the next traveler. A lookout can repay that knowledge with a dated change to a route elsewhere.

name: Let the bait choice say which interruption is acceptable

gm.title: At the table
