lines: Mounted riders accuse a ship of crossing a boundary. The ship stayed on its declared course. The tritons can show that the marker stones moved after the latest tide.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Trolls serve tea after collecting the bridge toll. A regular knows which herb signals that the bridge is unsafe and who taught the trolls to use it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Anyone can talk safely inside the inn after surrendering arms. A bell tells everyone when a surrendered item is moved, including the one a guest needs to get home.

name: Two apprentices inherit the same unfinished tattoo

gm.title: At the table
lines: A retired artist drew half a commemorative piece before losing their steady hand. Each apprentice can complete a different missing part. The client must choose whether to keep it unfinished, share the commission, or accept one drawing that changes its meaning.

name: Two caches hold the same key blank

gm.title: At the table
lines: A key in a flooded lockbox and another in a dry wall cavity share their cut but have different maker's marks. Trying either at the gate works. Comparing the marks can show who copied the lock before the authorities replaced it, which changes who can be trusted to guard it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An heir and a jeweler each have paperwork for the same valuable ring. One document claims the metal and the other the stone.

name: Two drip trays date a switch

gm.title: At the table
lines: Red and white candles were lit together over numbered trays. A fireman opened a service hatch halfway through the watch, sending both flames sideways. The party can compare the order of straight and sideways wax streaks to tell whether the labeled trays were switched before or after the hatch opened.

name: Two fair winds meet on a saddle

gm.title: At the table
lines: Winds blow toward the same saddle from opposite valleys. The dry grass shows the boundary shifting during the day. A caravan with a sail-powered cart can wait for the winds to line up with the descent or furl the sail and haul the cart down with ropes.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A noble's death is celebrated at one gate and mourned at another. Each procession believes theirs has the body.

name: Two neighborhood contests share one prize

gm.title: At the table
lines: One crowd awards the trophy for the fastest completion, and the other for the tidiest work. The same carpenter is judging both. Let the party choose which standard to endorse or build another trophy instead of taking the first.

name: Two plans contradict an architect’s alibi

gm.title: At the table
lines: A Plan-reader lamp flickers at different doorways on each submitted plan. One drawing gives someone a route from the street past the locked entrance. Ask who paid for the intervening renovation, or try the route before the owner notices the check.

name: Two rival associations pay for the same footpath

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each pays for a different half and saws through its posts when the other falls behind. A flood has temporarily shifted the midpoint. The party can broker shared upkeep or learn where the joint account still has funds.

name: Two satyrs disagree about the joke

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two performers have wagered something they cannot afford to lose. A party member can judge fairly or find a target both would rather tease.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Rival bars each brew one half of a drink. Both halves must reach the bridge before the ferryman opens the crossing, and tonight the brewers are feuding.

name: Two tattoo portraits disagree about the span

gm.title: At the table
lines: A clerk reproduced the prisoner's mark beside a standard door bolt on the same forearm. A new impression appears larger and carries the same bolt. Compare their proportions to establish whether the whole image was resized or the mark belongs to someone else.

name: Two versions of a town square

gm.title: At the table
lines: A rift brings the past and future to the same square at different hours. A resident from each era asks the party to change the same decision for opposite reasons.

name: Two wizards divided by a wall

gm.title: At the table
lines: Rival spellcasters cast alternating wards that push the same shared wall back and forth. The neighbors can show which side first broke the old agreement.

name: Unlisted riders use the back trough

gm.title: At the table
lines: The caretaker marks a cup with the stable brand of each served rider. Three brands never appear in the guestbook. Help the keeper watch the back trough to find which riders are being admitted after closing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Set one pre-adventure action in a location the party can visit for a present reason. Let a repair, stain, or changed routine reveal what happened there.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Record when the triggering incident occurred, who benefited, and which NPC acted first afterward. Give each fact a different way to reach the table in case the intended meeting falls through.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An insular bar lets outsiders in when they can name a practical gift the regulars need. A banned patron waits nearby with good advice and an ulterior motive.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A group covers city statues in paint that washes off at noon. Under it, older layers prove the city had changed each dedication before.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A small creature shelters inside a boot left out to dry. The party can follow its retreat to discover where their guide hid the spare boots.

name: Vines label the paths as water rises

gm.title: At the table
lines: Trailing vines cling to trunks horizontally at the previous flood's highest level. Compare the newest leaf growth with the line to decide which ridge remains above water. An older mark shows where the safer-looking ridge used to wash out.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Everyone who drinks sees the same broken bridge from a different angle. Assemble the descriptions to locate it before the wagons take that route.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A creature's mouth moves and its speech emerges from a loose board elsewhere in the room. A whisper into a crack beside the board reaches the creature alone.

name: Voice with the weight of a drum

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker's low voice carries through floorboards. A listener below can recognize the speaker even if the words remain unclear.

name: Wall flowers open where air circulates

gm.title: At the table
lines: Pale blooms open by a cracked lintel and stay folded in sealed rooms. Recognizing the difference gives explorers a way to find the only passage where several people can work safely for hours.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Wargs test one gate every night and break off when its bell sounds. The bell ringer has an offer to miss a shift.

name: Warm a building by unwinding one knot

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cloth stores a room's warmth in a row of knots. Unwind one to warm a new room for an hour and chill the corresponding area of the original building. Ask who still needs the old room before using the last knot.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A guard invites one member to answer a routine complaint. A court clerk offers to show the docket to the others while the officer is out.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Thick strands tie a door to its frame from both sides. One creature is inside with something that keeps moving the latch.

name: Who keeps the molds when the furnace cools

gm.title: At the table
lines: The departing tenant is allowed to break the old molds after turning off the furnace. A buyer needs their profiles for a licensed repair. Include the originals in the handoff, copy the profiles before shutoff, or find who still has the original drawings.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Unending twilight ends briefly around a transferred relic. Farmers, navigators, and nocturnal citizens each offer a use for those few minutes.

name: Why the harpies left their island

gm.title: At the table
lines: A flock nesting in harbor blocks safe passage. They will move if the party recovers eggs left on their old island. The harbormaster is willing to move shipping for a day if someone can prove the flock plans to leave.

name: Wild kin on a disputed trail

gm.title: At the table
lines: A band maintains a path outsiders claim was empty for decades. Old repairs in their distinctive style prove regular use.

name: Win the handoff without winning the whole race

gm.title: At the table
lines: Mark three points where different couriers can trade the parcel. A player can skip a segment by committing to a wrong-way risk now, or watch one transfer and use that information for the next.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A jar contains wind that blows in the direction it was bottled. Loose paper twists toward the coast printed on the seller's label.

name: Words of ownership pull at the ground

gm.title: At the table
lines: Saying that you own a parcel of land makes your next step on it heavy. Asking permission from anyone who lives there restores an easy stride until dawn. Try making a claim first with one foot across the boundary.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Describe the factions, debts, or locations that would carry forward under several plausible outcomes. Ask which survivors, obligations, or places the players want to spend another session with.

name: Yesterday's collateral needs to be used today

gm.title: At the table
lines: A pawnbroker has taken a ferry token as collateral and would lend it under supervision. Only the borrower knows how to seat it in the old ferry gate. The party can guarantee its return while the two travel together.

name: +1 All-Purpose Tool
summary: Change between artisan's tools and loan the artificer a cantrip.

name: A History of Dragons and Drakes
summary: Separates named specimens and their habitats from sailors' tales.

name: Accordion-fold music stand
summary: A wooden stand collapses into a narrow bundle between two leather straps.

name: Acid (vial)
summary: One dose sold in its throw-ready container.

name: Adamantine ore
summary: Unrefined stock for a smith who can work adamantine.

name: Adjustable cuff bands (pair)
summary: Hold sleeves in place for a fitting without stitches.

name: Adjustable shelf index strips
summary: Short tags slide into one long rail to mark the current contents of a shared shelf.

name: Afterrain sugar stems
summary: The stems have a crisp sweet center. Buy them cut and sealed for the morning market.

name: Airing peg
summary: Fasten it to wet fabric and it rings once when that fold is dry all the way through. It dries nothing by itself.

name: Alchemist's Fire (flask)
summary: A single-use flask of persistent flame.

name: Alchemy Jug
summary: Produce one of its listed liquids each day.

name: Alexandrite
summary: A cut gem that can appear a different color under different light.

name: Amber piece
summary: A small piece of hardened golden resin.

name: Ambersprout
summary: A sweet root whose rind releases tacky sap useful on a torn bandage.

name: Amulet of the Drunkard
summary: Once a day, drinking alcohol can restore some hit points.

name: An Advocate's Phrasebook
summary: Summarizes common objections and the documents a hearing clerk asks to see.

name: Anchor patch tattoo
summary: Touch a clean cloth to the fresh mark to copy its outline once. Compare that outline to the skin later to check whether the tattoo stretched during a transformation.

name: Apple cider
summary: A drink pressed from apples.

name: Apples (three)
summary: Three apples sold as a small bundle.

name: Apricot hand tart
summary: Small folded pastry with an apricot center and a firm seam.

name: Arcane focus orb
summary: A polished sphere a spellcaster can hold as an arcane focus.

name: Arcane focus rod
summary: A short rigid rod made to serve as an arcane focus.

name: Arcane focus wand
summary: A narrow hand-held wand made to serve as an arcane focus.

name: Arctic tracks handbook
summary: Shows tracks in fresh snow and common changes after a thaw.

name: Arrow-Catching Shield
summary: Protect nearby allies from some ranged weapon attacks.

name: Atomizer bulb and bottle
summary: Dispenses a mist from a thin liquid. A spare bulb fits the same neck.

name: Attar blending kit
summary: Four single-note sample oils plus separate empty bottles for trying combinations.

name: Attic key
summary: Turns only when the person carrying it has climbed higher than everyone else in the building.

name: Awl sleeve
summary: A leather guard keeps a sharp awl from piercing the tool roll.

name: Azurite
summary: A low-cost deep-blue stone.

name: Backstamp book press
summary: Press one volume without opening its cover to get an impression of the binder's most recent mark from inside the spine.

name: Backward quill
summary: Writes legibly only on the reverse of a sheet.

player.title: Capacity and handling
lines: The bag can carry up to 500 pounds and 64 cubic feet. It weighs 15 pounds regardless of what it holds.
Taking an item out requires an action. Overloading, piercing, or tearing the bag destroys it and scatters its contents into the Astral Plane.

name: Bagpipes
summary: Suited to marching and performances outdoors.

name: Bailing scoop with deck hook
summary: A bent lip rests its handle over a rail so the scoop stays easy to reach.

name: Banquet place setting
summary: A meal for one person at a prepared feast.

name: Barley bread
summary: A plain, dense bread made with barley.

name: Barn owl face
summary: Hear a whisper through a single thin partition while both feet remain planted.

name: Barnacle face
summary: Walk across still water for one minute. Each footfall leaves a visible ring even in darkness.

name: Barrelstalk
summary: A hollow fungus sold sealed with a wax plug. A fresh one holds a day's water for two travelers.

name: Barrier Tattoo (Small)
summary: While attuned and unarmored, use AC 12 plus Dexterity modifier. A shield still works.

name: Barter bakewell
summary: A tart is baked with a second empty shell inside. A buyer can tuck in their own tiny gift before passing it along.

name: Basket
summary: Open carry basket for produce, pottery, or loose supplies.

name: Bat guano (1 lb)
summary: A pound of dried bat droppings sold as a spell component.

name: Battering Shield
summary: Turn a successful shove into a stronger displacement.

name: Bean flour (1 lb)
summary: Thickens stew and travels well in a dry sack.

name: Beeswax bowl covers (set)
summary: Cloth covers seal three different sizes of bowl.

name: Bell with two clappers
summary: Either clapper can be pinned independently, making two recognizable signals with the same bell.

name: Belt
summary: An adjustable waist strap that can carry a pouch or sheath.

name: Bench vise
summary: Clamps to the side of a sturdy worktable.

name: Bent seam ruler
summary: A fixed curve is convenient for tracing the same rounded shape many times.

name: Binding thread bobbin
summary: Strong, smooth cotton thread to rebind a small book.

name: Bismuth crystal
summary: A stepped, metallic-looking crystal with shifting surface colors.

name: Black pearl
summary: A 100 gp specimen for component shopping. Check the spell’s minimum value.

name: Blackberry fruit leather
summary: Tart strips rolled in wax paper.

name: Blank appointment oval
summary: A recipient can press a handwritten appointment slip against the oval to move the entry onto their skin. A second slip replaces it, and soap clears the oval.

name: Blood sausage links
summary: A string of dark sausages made with blood and seasoning.

name: Bloodroot
summary: A portion of reddish plant root stocked by the apothecary.

name: Blue agate worry bead
summary: One side is polished smooth. The other preserves the curve of the raw stone.

name: Bluecap flour (1 lb)
summary: A blue flour for making bread where grain is scarce.

name: Boneknob
summary: Its hard rind can be carved like a low-grade piece of horn.

name: Boots
summary: Ankle-covering footwear for road and field work.

name: Boots of Elvenkind
summary: Quiet the wearer's footsteps.

name: Boots of False Tracks
summary: Leave prints belonging to a different humanoid of the same size.

name: Boots of the Winterlands
summary: Footwear for cold environments and snowy travel.

name: Borrowed-key gauge
summary: A loose scale and small clamps preserve a key's profile for comparison while leaving the key usable.

name: Bottled melody
summary: Plays the tune held inside when uncorked and empties after use.

name: Bracket drip tray
summary: Hooks under a wall bracket and slides out for cleaning without moving the candle.

name: Brass wind chimes
summary: Suspended brass pieces that ring when moved by the wind.

name: Breathing Bubble
summary: Maintain breathable air around the wearer's head.

name: Brimstone (1 lb)
summary: A pound of yellow sulfur sold as a component.

name: Broken sweet sack
summary: An affordable paper bag filled from pieces chipped at the counter that day.

name: Brooch of Shielding
summary: Protect against force damage and magic missile.

name: Broom
summary: A bundle of stiff sweeping fibers secured to a long handle.

name: Brown ale
summary: A darker ale with a malt-forward taste.

name: Brown bream string
summary: Five small bony fish for stock and pickling.

name: Brushes for long and short winter coats
summary: Two brushes have different bristle lengths and distinct handles.

name: Bubble wand
summary: Makes one bubble large enough to carry a sealed written note over water.

name: Bucket
summary: Useful for drawing water, bailing, or carrying rubble.

name: Burglar's Pack
summary: Ready-packed supplies for a break-in. Check the source for contents.

name: Burial index
summary: Newly written names point to graves with a location recorded in the book. Unrecorded burials leave the page blank.

name: Butter biscuits
summary: Crumbly biscuits flavored with butter.

name: Butter-braised leeks
summary: Soft leeks served cold in a shallow plate with a bread end.

name: Cabbage head
summary: One firm head of cabbage.

name: Calibrated scale weights
summary: Spare weights from one ounce to one pound, stamped to verify a scale with a known load.

name: Calligrapher's Supplies
summary: Tools for professional lettering and inscription.

name: Camel
summary: A pack or riding mount suited to dry routes.

name: Camp water dipper
summary: A long hooked handle can reach inside a barrel and hang on its rim.

name: Candied fennel envelope
summary: Tiny sugar-coated seeds served after a heavy meal.

name: Candle of the Deep
summary: Gives light while submerged instead of going out.

name: Canted water jar
summary: Its ceramic foot rights itself to stand on a tilting bench while the jar is half full or less.

name: Canvas (1 sq. yd.)
summary: Heavy cloth for bags, awnings, and sail repairs.

name: Canvas roll
summary: A roll of heavy woven cloth for coverings, sacks, or patching.

name: Canvas shade sling
summary: Four loops and a shallow cut let a pair of travelers pitch shade without using a whole tent.

name: Cap of Water Breathing
summary: Breathe underwater while wearing the cap.

name: Cape
summary: A sleeveless outer layer that hangs from the shoulders.

name: Caravan muster ribbon
summary: Long ribbon with hand loops for keeping a caravan together in poor visibility.

name: Care and Feeding of Familiars
summary: Explains ordinary feeding and rest for common familiar shapes.

name: Carriage
summary: Enclosed passenger transport with seating and shelter.

name: Carrot bunch
summary: A tied bunch of fresh carrots.

name: Carved drinking cup
summary: A drinking cup with a carved exterior and a firm grip.

name: Celestial blood (vial)
summary: A sealed vial of blood from a celestial creature.

name: Censer
summary: A bowl or hanging vessel for burning incense.

name: Chalcedony
summary: A pale, translucent carving stone.

name: Chalk marking string
summary: Snaps a straight line onto cloth, stone, or timber.

name: Chalk trace wallet
summary: Stiff sleeves keep four labeled rubbings apart and catch the dust from friable marks.

name: Charcoal (1 lb)
summary: A pound of charred wood for drawing, fuel, or mixing.

name: Chariot
summary: A light, open vehicle for fast travel on level ground.

name: Charlatan's Die
summary: The attuned holder can choose how it lands.

name: Chime of Opening
summary: Open doors or containers from a distance using a limited number of charges.

name: Cinch purse
summary: Open the purse and add coins. Closing it moves the new coins into a separate inner pocket. You may remove that batch the next time you open it. Unremoved coins join the main pile when you shut it again.

name: Cinnabar
summary: Red mineral pigment for an illuminator's palette.

name: Cinnamon
summary: Sold by the pound.

name: Citrus basket
summary: A market basket of assorted citrus fruit.

name: Citrus hair pomade
summary: Keeps loose hair down under a hat.

name: Clamp-on step
summary: A folding foothold clamps to a stout square rail when a ladder needs its last rung replaced.

name: Cleansing Stone
summary: Remove dirt and grime from a creature and its clothing.

name: Cloak of Elvenkind
summary: Helps the wearer hide from observers using sight.

name: Cloak of Many Fashions
summary: Change the cloak's style, color, and apparent quality.

name: Cloak of the Manta Ray
summary: Swim and breathe underwater while its hood is up.

name: Cloakroom countertoken
summary: Divide it in two before leaving one with an attendant. Neither half may be sold or traded while the other remains in that attendant's keeping.

name: Clockwork Amulet
summary: Once per day, use a fixed attack roll of 10 before modifiers.

name: Clockwork mask
summary: Once per dawn, store a natural 1 or 20 you roll. Before the next dawn, a willing creature you touch can take that result for its next d20 roll. It must choose before rolling. The dial then clears.

name: Cloth hook guard
summary: A sewn guard folds around a baited hook between casts.

name: Clothes of Mending
summary: Repair small rips and tears in the garment over time.

name: Clothesline gauge
summary: Two folding legs show how much clearance a sagging line will leave above a low fence.

name: Cloud macaron
summary: Spirals upward if dropped and falls again when it cools.

name: Cloud mallet
summary: Strikes a gavel block without sound and leaves a puff marking the point of impact.

name: Cloves
summary: Sold by the pound.

name: Cobalt ore
summary: Unrefined ore sold by the mineral merchant for its cobalt content.

name: Cobbled folding seat
summary: Replaced hinges keep the seat upright. The legs have two different splay angles and each foot is numbered.

name: Coiling Grasp Tattoo
summary: Extend a magical grip at range.

name: Coin of Delving
summary: Drop it to estimate the depth of a hole or shaft.

name: Coin rubbing sleeve
summary: Holds a single copper piece still while a buyer rubs its face onto paper.

name: Cold-run salmon collar
summary: A fatty cut sold with the bones intact for cooking over coals.

name: Collapsible sawhorse
summary: The legs swing flat for carrying or stacking.

name: Color shift tiles
summary: A set of glazed tiles gives a stable comparison when an ink or dye changes as it dries.

name: Colored bulb sleeve
summary: A colored glass jacket slips around an enclosed lantern. Signalers can swap sleeves without changing the flame.

name: Common bird feather
summary: A single ordinary feather suitable for a component pouch.

name: Common Glamerweave
summary: Cloth with a moving decorative illusion.

name: Component Pouch
summary: Holds ordinary spell components. Buy specific components separately when a spell calls for them.

name: Cooking utensils
summary: Shared utensils for cooking over a campfire.

name: Copper ingot (1 lb)
summary: A one-pound cast bar of reddish copper for metalwork or trade.

name: Coralsprout
summary: Grows near hot vents. Cuts of the chilled root go soft and pink.

name: Corner crease clip
summary: Closes on two folded pages without piercing either one.

name: Corner sighting prism
summary: The narrow housing fits in a half-open door and shows what's around the jamb.

name: Cotton candy ration
summary: Weighs almost nothing, but dissolves in the rain.

name: Cotton Cloth (1 sq. yd.)
summary: Light cloth for garments and linings.

name: Cotton wick braid (yard)
summary: Wide flat braid fits a standard bench lamp.

name: Countermark tattoo
summary: Adds a second matching pattern when two willing bearers press their marks together for a minute. The second pattern lasts until dawn.

name: Counterweight cage
summary: An iron basket with marked slots holds test weights while a crew adjusts a stubborn pulley.

name: Counterweight clasp
summary: Clasp it to both ends of a strap. The ends feel equally heavy in your hands. The heavier side can still pull the strap and whatever it carries off balance.

name: Courgette pie
summary: A savory pastry filled with sliced courgettes.

name: Courgettes (three)
summary: Three courgettes sold together.

name: Courtship sachets (pair)
summary: Each cloth envelope holds the same scent. The seller will seal a name or small note inside either one.

name: Covered wagon
summary: A canvas-covered trade wagon priced on the same scale as an ordinary wagon.

name: Cow
summary: One live cow.

name: Crab hamper with double lid
summary: An inner slatted grate can stay shut while the outer lid is left open to feed a crab.

name: Crate
summary: A sturdy slatted box for stacking or carrying goods.

name: Creamed parsnip crocks (two)
summary: Two small hot earthenware bowls meant to be shared.

name: Credit chalk and slate
summary: Choose two willing people. When one awards the other a written tally on the slate, the same number is marked on the recipient's chalk stub. Washing the slate ends the agreement.

name: Creel divider
summary: Keeps bait and catch in separate parts of one basket.

name: Crossbow Bolt Case
summary: Holds crossbow ammunition separately from an arrow quiver.

name: Crucible sling
summary: A loose metal cradle lets two people walk a cool crucible down stairs without tilting it.

name: Crystalheart
summary: A slice clouds in contact with fouled water.

name: Cucumbers (three)
summary: Three cucumbers sold together.

name: Cushioned tracing pad
summary: A washable pad collects pressure marks on soft chalk so a harness can be adjusted before the next day's ride.

name: Darts (10)
summary: Ten small weighted throwing darts packed together.

name: Deadline-release clip
summary: Agree on an hour with a second person. Attach the clip to the flap of a document wallet. After that hour, the clip opens for either participant. Before then, both must hold it.

name: Debtwitness seal box
summary: Press one document against the bottom to record its outline and total number of seals. The next document can be checked against both. The box displays no words.

name: Decanter of Endless Water
summary: Issue a stream or a forceful jet of water by command.

name: Deck creel rack
summary: A board with pegs and a drain slot holds fish baskets off the deck.

name: Deck tally sliders
summary: Ten painted beads run on a wire fixed to the rail for counting baskets as they come aboard.

name: Delivery crock with a witness groove
summary: Press a fresh seal into its groove. Until the lid is removed, the groove preserves the last shape it touched even if the seal breaks in transit.

name: Dew catch for a feed rack
summary: A shallow slanted cover keeps condensation out of a salt or feed bin.

name: Diamond
summary: A 1,000 gp specimen for component shopping. Check the spell’s minimum value.

name: Diamond dust
summary: A packet of finely powdered diamond sold by the component merchant.

name: Dinner with a Mimic
summary: An illustrated farce with an unexpectedly accurate index of habits.

name: Directing a Witness
summary: A clerk's handbook with diagrams for placing observers where they can reconstruct the same event.

name: Disguise Kit
summary: Supplies for changing a person's outward appearance.

name: Dishcloth of clear water
summary: Wring the cloth over a basin. The first liquid it absorbed since it last dried falls separately from whatever it absorbed later.

name: Doorstep tally tile
summary: Set it on a single step. For one day its chalk mark rises by one each time someone lifts the tile. It cannot count creatures that step around it.

name: Double-mouth serving pitcher
summary: A wide lip pours from either side while the server holds the center handle.

name: Dovetail tapers (pair)
summary: If the two flames come within a handbreadth, one extinguishes and the other doubles in height until the candles are separated.

name: Draft threads
summary: Six short lengths of contrasting silk on clay tabs for reading weak airflow around a frame.

name: Dragon blood (vial)
summary: A sealed vial of blood from a dragon.

name: Dragon scale shard
summary: A broken piece of a large dragon scale.

name: Drawknife saddle
summary: Light clamping board catches a workpiece against a bench while a drawknife is pulled.

name: Dream admission ticket
summary: Lets one willing sleeper follow a companion into the same dream.

name: Dream biscuit
summary: The taste recalls the last meal you shared with someone.

name: Dreamweaver root
summary: Eat a cooked piece alongside an unfamiliar dish and that night you dream of the last ingredient added to the dish.

name: Dressed chicken
summary: A plucked, cleaned chicken ready for cooking.

name: Dried beans (sack)
summary: A sack of dry beans for soaking and cooking.

name: Dried moss (1 lb)
summary: A pound of dried moss packed loose for the component bench.

name: Dried mushroom assortment
summary: Three edible sorts in separate paper sleeves.

name: Dried peas (sack)
summary: A sack of dried peas for soups, stews, and storage.

name: Dried plums (packet)
summary: Enough fruit for two breakfasts.

name: Dried scallop fan
summary: Four scallops wrapped separately to keep them from sticking.

name: Dried smelt pouch
summary: A handful of thin preserved fish. Good for a trail snack or bait.

name: Driftglobe
summary: Carry a light that can float beside the party.

name: Drip clock flask
summary: Fill to the mark and hang in a cold room. A magical latch shuts at the first freeze and holds the reading even if the flask thaws. The level records how long the room stayed above freezing. Reset by removing the stopper.

name: Drowsy shield
summary: Softens sound when set upright between a sleeper and a doorway.

name: Dry cedar shaving oil
summary: Sold with a scrap of the same wood so soap and shaving oil can be matched.

name: Dusk cabbage
summary: Outer leaves darken as the light drops.

name: Dust of Deliciousness
summary: Flavors up to six servings. Gives diners disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saves for 1 hour.

name: Dust of Disappearance
summary: A single-use way to hide several nearby creatures at once.

name: Dust of Dryness
summary: Turn a large amount of water into a pellet that can be broken later.

name: Eagle feather
summary: A large feather with a stiff central shaft.

name: Echo crystal
summary: Leave it on a hard surface to record the next clear sound in the room. Tap it twice to play that sound back and erase it.

name: Eel stew
summary: Chunks of eel simmered in broth and served warm.

name: Efficient Quiver
summary: A magic quiver with separate spaces for ammunition, bows, and long shafts.

name: Eggs with bacon
summary: Cooked eggs served alongside cured bacon.

name: Eldritch Claw Tattoo
summary: Enhance unarmed attacks and briefly extend their reach.

name: Electrum ingot (1 lb)
summary: A one-pound bar of pale gold-silver alloy.

name: Elephant
summary: Carries heavy freight on routes that accommodate its size.

name: Elixir of Health
summary: Carry an answer to a selection of disabling conditions.

name: Emberspine root
summary: Stays warm enough to warm cold hands for one watch.

name: Embroidered pillowcase
summary: A fabric pillow cover decorated with stitched patterns.

name: Emerald Pen
summary: Write without ink or cast Illusory Script without material components.

name: Enduring Spellbook
summary: A spellbook built to withstand fire, water, and time.

name: Entertainer's Pack
summary: Ready-packed equipment for a traveling performer.

name: Everbright Lantern
summary: Provides steady illumination without burning oil.

name: Eversmoking Bottle
summary: Produce enough smoke to break sightlines.

name: Eye of newt
summary: A small preserved newt eye kept in the apothecary’s stock.

name: Eyes of Minute Seeing
summary: Inspect small details at close range.

name: Eyes of the Eagle
summary: Spot visual details at long range.

name: Facet visor
summary: See all around for as long as you stand still. Taking a step ends the view.

name: Faded portrait
summary: A blurred likeness that clears when the subject stands in sunlight.

name: Felt roll
summary: A rolled length of matted wool cloth.

name: Fermentation jar with weight
summary: A flat ceramic disk holds vegetables below the brine.

name: Ferryvine marker tape
summary: A field cord woven from vine bast. Once wet, its pale stripes are visible against dark or muddy branches.

name: Festival spindle ribbon
summary: A pre-cut ribbon with reinforced ends for tying to a portable frame.

name: Fiend heart
summary: A preserved fiend heart sold as a rare component.

name: Fire lichen strip
summary: Hold it to rock for a minute. The fringe curls toward the warmest point of contact.

name: Fire Opal
summary: A bright stone for high-value jewelry or trade.

name: Fire poker
summary: A long iron rod for shifting embers and logs in a hearth.

name: First-hour perfume
summary: Changes through three distinct scents over one hour. Patrons at formal evenings sometimes coordinate their visits around the changes.

name: Fish bait vial
summary: Empty it on the surface and nearby fish gather around the spot for a minute.

name: Fishing floats (six)
summary: A mix of narrow and broad cork shapes for still or moving water.

name: Fishing Tackle
summary: A kit for catching a meal where fishing is possible.

name: Fitting stripe tattoo
summary: The stripe appears at its usual length whenever the wearer straightens their arm. Hours later they can use the same line to verify a copied measurement.

name: Five-tap counting baton
summary: The first four taps sound only to the holder. The fifth sounds aloud and resets the count.

name: Flailfish pair
summary: A mild white fish. The stallholder sells pairs for cooks who want two equal portions.

name: Flask of wine
summary: A stoppered flask of table wine that fits in a travel pack.

name: Flat seam press
summary: A hard-edged wooden block holds flattened fabric while the tailor works the next crease.

name: Flexible mirror stalk
summary: A very small polished disk on a bendable stem shows the back of a gear housing.

name: Floating wick disks (four)
summary: Each holds a short wick at the surface of a little bowl of oil.

name: Floor key rest
summary: A cast stand catches a long key above table height so someone can compare cut depths hands-free.

name: Fog music box
summary: Uneven notes play while low mist gathers inside the lid.

name: Fog sugar lace
summary: A delicate white sweet stays crisp in dry air and collapses when the party crosses into a noticeably wetter pocket.

name: Folded chalk tray
summary: A pair of leather flaps catch chalk dust and open to empty it.

name: Folding Boat
summary: Carry a small box and deploy it as a boat when needed.

name: Forgery Kit
summary: Tools for producing convincing credentials and documents.

name: Fossil rib
summary: A partial rib from a creature larger than a wagon.

name: Fossil shell
summary: A spiral shell found far above the present coastline.

name: Four-person tent
summary: A canvas field shelter with room for four sleepers.

name: Freestanding doorframe
summary: Opens onto a dark, shallow alcove big enough to hide a single pack.

name: Fresh cod
summary: Fresh white-fleshed cod for the pot or pan.

name: Fresh corn (three cobs)
summary: Three fresh ears of corn.

name: Fresh eel
summary: A fresh eel sold whole or ready to cut for cooking.

name: Fresh herring
summary: Fresh herring from the fish stall, sold without curing.

name: Fresh milk
summary: Milk sold for immediate use or cooking.

name: Fresh salmon
summary: Fresh salmon sold for cooking the same day.

name: Fried frog legs
summary: Frog legs fried and served as a hot dish.

name: Frost receipt film
summary: Press the film over a frosted surface. For one watch it holds an outline of any frost removed in the past hour.

name: Frostvein root
summary: Keeps a single small parcel chilled until it thaws.

name: Fruit cream tart
summary: A pastry shell filled with cream and topped with fruit.

name: Galley
summary: A long vessel with banks of oars for speed independent of the wind.

name: Garden staff level
summary: Sight through the level tube while two other people hold staffs on the marks. Compare the height where the line crosses each staff.

name: Garlic bulb
summary: A whole garlic bulb with its cloves still joined.

name: Garlic toast
summary: Toasted bread rubbed or seasoned with garlic.

name: Garment position diagram
summary: A thin template marks sleeve lengths and hem lines before cloth is cut.

name: Gear tooth gauge
summary: A set of ridged edges matches standard tooth spacing before a replacement is cut.

name: Ghoul-hide mantle
summary: While dry, it makes ghouls mistake your scent for that of a small member of their own kind.

name: Ginger
summary: Sold by the pound.

name: Gingerbread
summary: A spiced sweet baked with ginger.

name: Glazed chestnut roll
summary: A dark bread roll with chopped chestnut and a gloss of sugar.

name: Glazed dough trough
summary: Wide walls support folding dough on a low bench.

name: Gloomtide tuber
summary: The skin gives off a green glow when freshly cut.

name: Gloves
summary: Close-fitting hand coverings for travel and work.

name: Glowing cue card
summary: Draw up to three cue symbols. Touch one to make it glow for a minute.

name: Glowing dumpling
summary: A bite leaves a soft blue glow on the tongue for an hour.

name: Goat
summary: One live goat for a household or homestead.

name: Goblet fern tube
summary: The split stalk forms a sturdy channel. Two can be joined to carry a trickle of water across a short gap.

name: Goggles of Night
summary: Extend or provide darkvision for scouting.

name: Goggles of Object Reading
summary: Aid Arcana checks on visible creatures or objects and cast Identify once per dawn.

name: Gold ingot (1 lb)
summary: A one-pound cast bar of gold for trade or the jeweler’s bench.

name: Graduated dowry chain
summary: Each link carries its weight and can be sold at a different counter without cutting the chain.

name: Grain sampler
summary: Four handfuls of grain labeled so a buyer can test them before ordering a sack.

name: Grappling Hook
summary: Rig a line for a climb or haul.

name: Grave muster wand
summary: A bone can stand and walk toward the nearest other bone from its skeleton for one minute per dawn.

name: Grilled boar steak
summary: A cut of boar cooked over the grill and served hot.

name: Grilled spotted eelpout
summary: A whole fish split open and grilled with a sour glaze.

name: Grip gum (stick)
summary: Press chewed gum onto two clean hard surfaces. It holds a load until pulled sharply sideways, at which point the gum comes apart.

name: Hand Crossbow
summary: A compact crossbow that fires one-handed and needs a free hand to reload.

name: Hand pollination brush
summary: A soft dry brush in a sliding case keeps samples from touching between plants.

name: Hand-crank socket
summary: A replaceable square socket fits a short lever when a worn wooden crank splits.

name: Handbell for an empty chair
summary: Ring beside a chair and the bell repeats its tone when a living creature first sits there within the next hour. If the chair remains empty the bell stays quiet.

name: Handled soup cup
summary: Holds one serving and can be passed safely while warm.

name: Hanging seed pan
summary: Tiny holes drain water and keep seeds visible while starting.

name: Harbor favor chalk
summary: Mark an agreed dock post. Anyone who watched you make the mark can later find that post in dim light. Scrubbing the chalk off ends the effect.

name: Harmonica
summary: A pocket-sized reed instrument played by blowing and drawing air through it.

name: Harness keeper tabs
summary: Numbered leather tabs hold buckle settings while a team changes harnesses or trades animals.

name: Hat
summary: An everyday head covering for sun, rain, or cold.

name: Hat of Disguise
summary: Reuse a visual disguise for infiltration and social encounters.

name: Hat of Vermin
summary: A magician's hat that can produce small harmless animals.

name: Hazelnut cocoa spread
summary: A sweet spread of ground hazelnuts and cocoa.

name: Hearth caramel bar
summary: A slab of soft caramel with roasted oat crumbs.

name: Heat shield sleeve
summary: A stiff insulating sleeve keeps the side of a hot pot from touching its carrying strap.

name: Heat-tolerant nesting cup
summary: An open ceramic liner separates a small hot egg from combustible packing.

name: Heatproof bean pot

name: Shrinking cordial
summary: For ten minutes the drinker and their worn gear shrink enough to pass through a gap made for a house cat.

name: Side of pork
summary: A large butcher’s cut for portioning into smaller joints.

name: Sightline wax pellets (pair)
summary: Stick one pellet at a destination within a hundred paces. The other softens when pressed to a lit directional lantern that points directly at its mate.

name: Signal horn
summary: A hollow horn that carries a call across a camp, field, or stretch of road.

name: Signet Ring
summary: A personal seal for stamped correspondence.

name: Silk (1 sq. yd.)
summary: Fine cloth for dressmaking and decorative work.

name: Silk Rope (50 feet)
summary: A lighter alternative to the store's hemp rope.

name: Silk shirt
summary: A lightweight shirt of smooth woven silk.

name: Sill marker charm
summary: Mark a window latch and hold the charm. It makes the sound of the latch if the window opens before dawn within the same building.

name: Silver ingot (1 lb)
summary: A one-pound cast bar of silver for metalwork or trade.

name: Silver mirror
summary: A small mirror with a polished silver reflecting surface.

name: Skate stock block
summary: A compressed block flavored with skate and browned onion. Dissolve it in a pot of hot water.

name: Skinned rabbit
summary: A cleaned rabbit with the hide removed, ready for a stew or roast.

name: Sky jigsaw
summary: Holds one glimpse of the weather above the roof.

name: Slate brood marker
summary: A short foot stands on rough ground and the chalk face records the last turning.

name: Slate route tile
summary: Mark bearings and distances on a hand-sized tile, then wipe it clean for the next leg.

name: Sleepwalk slippers
summary: Track the wearer's route in faint chalk dust until dawn.

name: Slippers of Spider Climbing
summary: Free both hands while moving across suitable walls or ceilings.

name: Small ale
summary: A light, low-strength ale served as a table drink.

name: Small Doors and Narrow Halls
summary: A carpenter's sample book compares passage widths with familiar household objects.

name: Small object sample rig
summary: Holds a sample near the edge of a table for testing under different angles of light.

name: Smoked paprika tin
summary: The tight lid keeps the powder from perfuming the whole pack.

name: Smoky quartz
summary: A translucent quartz stone with a brown or gray tint.

name: Soap
summary: A bar for cleaning hands, clothing, or gear.

name: Soft aftercare wrap
summary: A washable cloth band with a loose weave and flat fastener.

name: Soft fence flag set
summary: Pale strips mark a temporary enclosure without a low wire.

name: Soft vise jaws
summary: Padded inserts grip finished wood or metal without marking it.

name: Sounding bobbin
summary: A weighted spool with color bands every five feet for measuring depth without committing a long rope.

name: Sour pickle crock
summary: Eight small cucumbers in brine. Repack them for travel to leave the crock in town.

name: Spare cog blanks (six)
summary: Uncut circular blanks match common small axle sizes.

name: Spare lute peg
summary: Rough-shaped hardwood with room for the buyer to fit the taper.

name: Spark drops (dozen)
summary: Crackling lights flash at the lips. Different flavors create different colors.

name: Spellshard
summary: Store writing in a crystal instead of on paper.

name: Spiced bun
summary: A soft bakery roll scented with warm spices.

name: Spider silk (1 oz)
summary: An ounce of fine spider thread wound together for storage.

name: Spinach tart
summary: An open savory tart filled with spinach.

name: Spinel
summary: A cut gem for jewelry or trade.

name: Spirit stone
summary: Warms within arm's reach of an incorporeal creature.

name: Splinter apron
summary: Dense felt along the pockets catches stray wood chips before they work into a worker's cuffs.

name: Split heir ring
summary: Two distinct rings interlock around a single stone. A buyer can wear either half separately.

name: Split hourglass
summary: Sand runs only while both halves are held by different people.

name: Split pea hand pie
summary: A baked folded crust with peas and pickled onion.

name: Split-rope turnout lead
summary: A forked last length attaches on both sides of a halter to spread pressure.

name: Spyglass
summary: Study an object, shoreline, or sail from a distance.

name: Stabling (per day)
summary: A night's berth and care for one mount.

name: Stacking water tins (three)
summary: Three square tins each hold a half gallon. They strap together on a pack frame without rolling.

name: Staff of Birdcalls
summary: Reproduce selected bird sounds to cue a friend or entertain a crowd.

name: Staff of Flowers
summary: Grow a flower from suitable ground using a charge.

name: Stage chime chain
summary: Three metal bars hang at different lengths and sound across a hall.

name: Star compass
summary: Points toward the last unobstructed view of the night sky.

name: Steel ingot (1 lb)
summary: A one-pound bar of steel stock for the forge.

name: Stern mooring pad
summary: A leather pad straps to a rope where it rubs over the back of a boat.

name: Stone of Good Luck
summary: A carried charm that improves checks and saves.

name: Stone setting sample board
summary: Shows twelve settings beside uncut stones of the same material.

name: Stormgem
summary: A cut root can make a nearby compass needle twitch.

name: Street Histories for New Apprentices
summary: Short maps show where trade halls stood before their names moved to different buildings.

name: Stretchable cloth hanger
summary: Two arms extend just far enough to support the shoulders of an ordinary garment, then retract when it is lifted.

name: Strong ale
summary: A fuller, stronger ale sold by the serving.

name: Studio arm rest
summary: A padded rest wedges in the gap between chair and table.

name: Sugarloaf
summary: A hard cone of sugar intended to be chipped into portions.

name: Sunfold fruit
summary: Its yellow peel opens a thumb's width in full daylight. Explorers set one near a chamber opening to tell whether daylight reaches it.

name: Sunforge tuber
summary: Mash a sun-ripened root into bread dough and it rises in the time it takes to pitch a tent.

name: Sunstone
summary: A warm orange or golden gemstone with a glint when turned in the light.

name: Survey chain repair links (six)
summary: Each tempered link is marked to match a standard chain interval.

name: Talking Doll
summary: Teach it phrases and set conditions for when it repeats them.

name: Tally dots
summary: Tap one of five dots in sequence to darken it. A long press on the first dot clears all five.

name: Tally floats
summary: Small numbered corks mark which containers drifted through a sluice or crossed a flood channel.

name: Tankard of Sobriety
summary: Drink alcohol from this vessel without getting drunk.

name: Tare washer
summary: Place it on the loaded pan of an ordinary balance beside an empty container and tap it once. It cancels its own weight and the weight of that container until it is lifted, so the balance measures anything added afterward.

name: Temporary hinge pin
summary: A stepped peg covers three common diameters for test-hanging a door.

name: Tent seam brush
summary: Pushes dust out of a fold before it can abrade stitched fabric.

name: Thank-you cake
summary: An inscription written in icing stays legible on every slice, even a slice cut before the message was added.

name: The Dark Below the Old Road
summary: A journal of a descent with notes on where the author turned back.

name: Theki Root
summary: Chew before an encounter where poison is expected.

name: Thickness gauge
summary: Transfers one measurement to multiple parts without reading a scale.

name: Thieves' Tools
summary: Fine tools for locks and mechanical traps.

name: Thread of opposite seams
summary: Split the length in half, sew a seam with each half, then tug one free. The other seam loosens at the same time. Useful for temporary fitting and stage clothes.

name: Three-Dragon Ante Set
summary: A dedicated deck for the named tavern game.

name: Three-generation mourning locket
summary: Three shallow frames fold out. Each takes a replacement portrait without disturbing the others.

name: Throat-rest mouthpiece
summary: A broad-lipped replacement cup for a short lip-blown horn.

name: Thunderstone
summary: A single-use signal stone that cracks with a thunderclap if dropped.

name: Tide reading slip board
summary: A float leaves a drawn maximum water level on a replaceable paper slip.

name: Tidewort
summary: A crisp cave vegetable that loses its briny flavor when dried.

name: Tile of two temperatures
summary: Two small piles of dust in its wells swap places whenever the left well becomes warmer than the right. Reset by brushing both clear.

name: Tin chorus mark
summary: One tap on the mark makes empty cups that touch the same wood tabletop ring softly. Activate it once before dawn.

name: Tin fuel funnel
summary: A narrow spout fits a lamp filler, and a hook holds the loose cap while you pour.

name: Titanium ore
summary: A mineral sample sold for its titanium content.

name: Tomatoes (basket)
summary: A small basket of fresh tomatoes.

name: Tongs
summary: Hinged metal grips for lifting items the smith cannot safely take by hand.

name: Trail Plants for City People
summary: Contrasts similar-looking plants using leaf shape, scent, and where they grow.

name: Transfer paper folio
summary: Holds twenty designs drawn in reverse for placing against skin.

name: Translucent plan folio
summary: Thin sheets take dark linework and can be overlaid for comparison.

name: Travel candle tube
summary: A long cap covers a candle so it can be carried beside clothing.

name: Travel jewel roll
summary: Divided suede pockets keep hard stones from scratching softer ones.

name: Travel stencil tube
summary: Spring clips hold several tacky transfer sheets under light tension so the sheets never touch in transit.

name: Traveler's Clothes
summary: A durable traveling outfit.

name: Treble chocolate
summary: For ten minutes the eater can hold a steady note even while moving or climbing.

name: Trial-fit price tag
summary: Attach it to an assembled sample. For one watch, the tag turns clear if the sample is taken apart and shows an outline of the first piece removed.

name: Trillimac cap sheet
summary: A dried sheet for wrapping something in a damp cavern.

name: Tuning hammer
summary: The shallow square socket grips a common zither or hammered-dulcimer peg.

name: Turned copper ear cuffs
summary: Clip over unpierced ears and come in matched pairs.

name: Turned-cuff tool wrap
summary: A rolled cloth keeps picks and small measures separate and lays flat for a count in poor light.

name: Turnips (sack)
summary: A sack of turnips for roasting, stewing, or storing.

name: Turnover copying board
summary: A hinged lower edge props a page up while leaving both hands free.

name: Twineleaf splint leaf (pair)
summary: The two leathery leaves stiffen when rubbed together. Fresh leaves conform to a shape before they harden.

name: Two-color parade sash
summary: Each side is one solid color so a marshal can signal a change by turning it over.

name: Two-color shoal spool
summary: One shade shows on dry line and a second shade appears on sections dipped in salt water. The mark stays after drying until washed with clear water.

name: Two-sided thaw patch
summary: Warms a cup placed on one side while icing a cup placed on the other. Peeling off the mark ends both effects.

name: Twohorn sculpin belly
summary: A small cut sold for simmering with root vegetables.

name: Unbleached dancer's gloves
summary: Thin, pale gloves with grippy cloth across the palm.

name: Uncertain egg
summary: The label insists it is a normal egg. Anything incubating it dreams of the creature that laid it.

name: Undecided forecast
summary: Seek counsel about one choice. The drink supplies a sound from one possible outcome without revealing which path made it happen.

name: Unicorn hair
summary: A strand of unicorn hair kept as a rare spell component.

name: Unicorn horn
summary: The spiral horn of a unicorn, prized as a rare component.

name: Unmeltable ice bonbon
summary: Snap apart the two halves. For a minute, each half tastes of the food or drink touching its counterpart.

name: Unscented wash powder
summary: Cleans clothes without leaving a fragrance.

name: Unspun wool (bag)
summary: A bag of loose wool ready for spinning or stuffing.

name: Used rolltop document case
summary: The clasp needs two hands. A replacement flap keeps papers dry in light rain.

name: Veilroot
summary: Steam from a cooked slice catches faint drafts at ground level.

name: Velvet vapor mask
summary: Once a day, turn to a wisp just long enough to pass through a loose grille. Anything in your hands stays behind.

name: Vinegar jug
summary: Pickling vinegar in a stoppered earthenware jug.

name: Vinegar mussel jar
summary: Mussels packed in sour vinegar and peppercorns.

name: Viol
summary: A bowed instrument sold with its bow.

name: Violin
summary: A bowed string instrument small enough for a traveling musician to carry.

name: Volunteer number panel
summary: A broad patch stitches onto a costume from the inside and can be removed afterward.

name: Wading staff grip
summary: A slotted grip slides halfway down a staff to help lean into the current.

name: Wand of Secrets
summary: Find the closest nearby secret door or trap with charges.

name: War wagon
summary: A reinforced wagon intended for use with a military convoy.

name: Warship
summary: A heavier vessel with room for fighters and supplies.

name: Watchful teddy
summary: A stitched bear that turns its head toward the first person to enter in the dark.

name: Waterorb pad
summary: A soft, spongy fungus for lifting small spills. Wring it out before reuse.

name: Waxed sample envelope (dozen)
summary: The folds close without glue and each holds a handful of dry seeds.

name: Waxed whipping thread (four spools)
summary: Four thicknesses of thread for binding the ends of cut ropes.

name: Wedge of hard cheese
summary: A portable piece of firm aged cheese.

name: Wedge pair with pull tabs
summary: Two shallow hardwood wedges can be withdrawn from the safe side by their cloth loops.

name: Weight tags (twenty)
summary: A waxed fold covers a dry square for writing a pack weight.

name: Weighted music clip
summary: A heavy clip holds open a music leaf outdoors.

name: Wet-weather gaiter clips (pair)
summary: Hold gaiters around the boot without a loose cord near the heel.

name: Wheat bread
summary: A wheat loaf for everyday meals and travel.

name: Whispering book
summary: Reads the facing page aloud when shut, once before dawn.

name: White flour (1 lb)
summary: A pound of sifted wheat flour for bread and pastry.

name: Whitevein fruit peel
summary: This naturally layered peel can be sewn into a glove for handling warm pots. The pale outer surface darkens where it needs replacing.

name: Wick threading hook
summary: Passes a replacement wick through a narrow burner neck.

name: Wild mushrooms (basket)
summary: A basket of foraged mushrooms sold by the greengrocer.

name: Willowshade Oil
summary: Ends petrification if applied within 1 minute of the creature becoming petrified.

name: Window candle for an agreed hour
summary: When lit, the candle sheds ordinary light indoors. From outdoors its light is visible through one chosen window only during the hour set when the candle was made, such as the first hour after dusk.

name: Winter blanket
summary: A thick woven blanket that can be folded into a bedroll.

name: Wire (10 ft)
summary: A coil of fine wire for tying fittings and making small repairs.

name: Witness brooch
summary: Its glass eye clouds when the wearer closes both real eyes.

name: Witness signature ladder
summary: A narrow ruler guides people to the next blank line when many names belong on one sheet.

name: Wolfsbane sprig
summary: A sprig of aconite stocked for component work.

name: Wooden practice clappers
summary: Two palm-sized boards for marking time without tuning an instrument.

name: Wool cap
summary: A close-fitting wool cap for cold days.

name: Wool hose
summary: Knitted or woven wool leg coverings.

name: Wool tunic
summary: A plain wool outer layer worn over a shirt.

name: Work apron
summary: A protective apron for a shopkeeper or craftsperson.

name: Work bowl with a level line
summary: A blue ring stays at the level of the liquid poured into the bowl. After a quick tilt, it stays at the last settled level for ten breaths.

name: Wrist audience line
summary: A set of three bars appears on the wrist while the wearer holds up a hand. The wearer can choose which bars to show. Lowering the hand conceals them.

name: Wyvern talon
summary: A hard curved claw from a wyvern, cleaned for the component trade.

name: Zinc dust (1 oz)
summary: An ounce of fine gray zinc powder in a sealed packet.

name: Zircon
summary: A comparatively affordable stone for a ring or pendant.

name: Zurkhwood plank
summary: Cut from a woody mushroom stem. It weighs less than a plank of oak the same size.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The aboleth can breathe air and water. Mucous Cloud. While underwater, the aboleth is surrounded by transformative mucus. A creature that touches the aboleth or that hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature is diseased for 1d4 hours. The diseased creature can breathe only underwater. Probing Telepathy. If a creature communicates telepathically with the aboleth, the aboleth learns the creature’s greatest desires if the aboleth can see the creature.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The aboleth makes three tentacle attacks. Tentacle. Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become diseased. The disease has no effect for 1 minute and can be removed by any magic that cures disease. After 1 minute, the diseased creature’s skin becomes translucent and slimy, the creature can’t regain hit points unless it is underwater, and the disease can be removed only by heal or another disease-curing spell of 6th level or higher. When the creature is outside a body of water, it takes 6 (1d12) acid damage every 10 minutes unless moisture is applied to the skin before 10 minutes have passed. Tail. Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft. one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. Enslave (3/Day). The aboleth targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed by the aboleth until the aboleth dies or until it is on a different plane of existence from the target. The charmed target is under the aboleth’s control and can’t take reactions, and the aboleth and the target can communicate telepathically with each other over any distance. Whenever the charmed target takes damage, the target can repeat the saving throw. On a success, the effect ends. No more than once every 24 hours, the target can also repeat the saving throw when it is at least 1 mile away from the aboleth.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The aboleth can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The aboleth regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Detect. The aboleth makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Swipe. The aboleth makes one tail attack. Psychic Drain (Costs 2 Actions). One creature charmed by the aboleth takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage, and the aboleth regains hit points equal to the damage the creature takes.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The aboleth can breathe air and water. Eldritch Restoration. If destroyed, the aboleth gains a new body in 5d10 days, reviving with all its Hit Points in the Far Realm or another location chosen by the GM. Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair). If the aboleth fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. Mucus Cloud. While underwater, the aboleth is surrounded by mucus. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the aboleth at the end of the aboleth’s turn. Failure: The target is cursed. Until the curse ends, the target’s skin becomes slimy, the target can breathe air and water, and it can’t regain Hit Points unless it is underwater. While the cursed creature is outside a body of water, the creature takes 6 (1d12) Acid damage at the end of every 10 minutes unless moisture is applied to its skin before those minutes have passed. Probing Telepathy. If a creature the aboleth can see communicates telepathically with the aboleth, the aboleth learns the creature’s greatest desires.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The aboleth makes two Tentacle attacks and uses either Consume Memories or Dominate Mind if available. Tentacle. Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 15 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of four tentacles. Consume Memories. Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature within 30 feet that is Charmed or Grappled by the aboleth. Failure: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The aboleth gains the target’s memories if the target is a Humanoid and is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this action. Dominate Mind (2/Day). Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the aboleth can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the aboleth dies or is on a different plane of existence from the target. While Charmed, the target acts as an ally to the aboleth and is under its control while within 60 feet of it. In addition, the aboleth and the target can communicate telepathically with each other over any distance. The target repeats the save whenever it takes damage as well as after every 24 hours it spends at least 1 mile away from the aboleth, ending the effect on itself on a success.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature’s turn, the aboleth can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The aboleth regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns. Lash. The aboleth makes one Tentacle attack. Psychic Drain. If the aboleth has at least one creature Charmed or Grappled, it uses Consume Memories and regains 5 (1d10) Hit Points.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The dragon can breathe air and water. Legendary Resistance (3/Day). If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The dragon can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws. Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) acid damage. Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage. Tail. Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. Frightful Presence. Each creature of the dragon’s choice that is within 120 feet of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature’s saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon’s Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours. Acid Breath (Recharge 5–6). The dragon exhales acid in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 54 (12d8) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The dragon can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Detect. The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Attack. The dragon makes a tail attack. Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions). The dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw or take 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

lines: Petrifying Gaze. If a creature starts its turn within 30 feet of the basilisk and the two of them can see each other, the basilisk can force the creature to make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw if the basilisk isn’t incapacitated. On a failed save, the creature magically begins to turn to stone and is restrained. It must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the creature is petrified until freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. A creature that isn’t surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can’t see the basilisk until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the basilisk in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. If the basilisk sees its reflection within 30 feet of it in bright light, it mistakes itself for a rival and targets itself with its gaze.

If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is instantly petrified. Otherwise, a creature that fails the save begins to turn to stone and is restrained.
